about: 실제 디자이너·연구 기관·디자인 시스템 팀의 무료 강의와 글에서 뽑은 규칙. 원문은 references/knowledge-*.md, 꺼내 보기는 scripts/knowledge.py

rules.rule: Pick the body face first, a plain legible face with tall x-height and open counters, before the display face.
rules.why: Body text has the tightest constraints.

rules.rule: Use clean neutral faces for most product and business UI; save distinctive faces for brands with strong personalities.
rules.why: Neutral faces keep content in front.

rules.rule: Do not use novelty fonts or faces that act out the theme, such as a spooky font for Halloween.
rules.why: They over-dramatise and look amateur.

rules.rule: Start from 3–5 brand adjectives and choose faces that subtly match them.
rules.why: Gives a checkable reason for every font choice.

rules.rule: Do not let overused default faces like Times New Roman or Arial carry the page; prefer a professionally made face.
rules.why: Upgrading the font is the single most visible improvement.

rules.rule: Treat a system UI stack (system-ui, -apple-system) as an acceptable plain token for product UI.
rules.why: Native rendering, zero download, variable weights on some OSes.

rules.rule: Choose the typeface before setting measure and line height.
rules.why: Metrics and widths differ by face, so spacing depends on it.

rules.rule: For data-heavy or financial UI, prefer a face that ships tabular figures.
rules.why: Live numbers must not jitter.

rules.rule: Use one family for most pages; two is fine, a third is rarely justified, four or more almost never.
rules.why: Size, weight and style already give enough variety.

rules.rule: Give each family one fixed job, e.g. A for headings and B for body, and write usage rules per element.
rules.why: Fixed roles keep hierarchy readable.

rules.rule: Switch fonts only at paragraph boundaries, never mid-paragraph.
rules.why: Mid-paragraph switches look like errors.

rules.rule: If you add a second family, make it contrast clearly; serif+sans when unsure, two sans only if width or structure differ clearly.
rules.why: Readers see a near-miss as a mismatch.
rules.conflict: Kennedy: ~95% of good pairs are serif+sans (S4); Butterick: similar faces often pair better (S1)

rules.rule: Define two typeface tokens (brand, plain) and map every type role to one of them.
rules.why: Changing fonts later becomes a two-token edit.

rules.rule: Set web running text at 15–25 px and never below 16 px; smaller sizes are for captions and footnotes only.
Set mobile body at 16–20 px on text-heavy pages and 16–18 px on interaction-heavy pages; start at 17 px.
rules.values: 16–20 px text-heavy; 16–18 px interaction-heavy; start 17 px

rules.rule: Set desktop body at 18–24 px for reading pages and 14–20 px for dense app UI.
Make form input text at least 16 px.
rules.why: iOS Safari zooms the page into smaller inputs.

rules.rule: Sanity-check body size against system defaults: Material 16, iOS 17 pt, GOV.UK 19, KRDS 17, Toss TDS 17.
rules.values: Material body-large 16 px; iOS body 17 pt (min 11 pt); GOV.UK 19 px; KRDS 17 px; TDS 17 px
rules.why: Use these as sanity anchors.

rules.rule: Set secondary text about 2 px smaller than body and lighter in colour.
Use about four sizes on a simple page: title, default, secondary, optional caption.
rules.why: More sizes blur hierarchy.

rules.rule: If a mobile line holds fewer than about 30 characters, reduce the body size.
rules.values: < ~30 chars per mobile line = too large

rules.rule: Size light or thin custom faces above the platform recommendations.
Build sizes from a defined scale exposed as tokens; never hard-code px per element.
rules.why: Tokens let text scale with user settings.

rules.rule: Copy a proven scale when needed, e.g. Material display, headline, title, body and label steps.
rules.values: display 57/45/36, headline 32/28/24, title 22/16/14, body 16/14/12, label 14/12/11 px

rules.rule: Carbon's scale steps can serve as a ready size ladder.
Define a small-screen and a large-screen type scale and interpolate between them; check the result at about 1024 px.
rules.values: e.g. ratio 1.2 at 320 px, 1.333 at 1500 px; check ~1024 px
rules.why: Removes breakpoint jumps.

rules.rule: Implement fluid sizes with clamp(min-rem, rem + vw, max-rem); never use vw alone.
rules.why: Pure vw blocks user zoom and resizing.

rules.rule: Set the page title at 28–40 px on mobile and 35–50 px on desktop.
rules.conflict: Butterick: document heads only slightly bigger than body; web systems use bigger steps

rules.rule: Keep headings about 1.25–1.5x body; never the same size as body unless weight sets them apart.
rules.conflict: Butterick: document heads only slightly bigger than body; web systems use bigger steps

rules.rule: Shrink headings on small screens as GOV.UK does, about 0.65–0.9x of their desktop size.
rules.values: xl 48(32), l 36(27), m 24(21), body 19, body-s 16 px; 80 px only exceptionally
rules.why: Shows how much headings shrink on mobile.

rules.rule: Use no more than three heading levels in running content; two is better.
Use compact productive styles in forms, tables and filters; expressive large styles only for page headers, banners and home pages.
rules.why: Never mix type sets inside one component.

rules.rule: Keep body lines at 45–90 characters including spaces, about 66 ideal; aim for 60–75 on desktop.
rules.why: Long lines make the return sweep to the next line hard.
rules.conflict: Ranges differ: 45–75 web.dev, 50–75 Kennedy, 60–80 Schöndorfer, 45–90 Butterick/USWDS

rules.rule: Set the measure with max-inline-size: 66ch (or about 30–40 rem), not a fixed px width.
rules.conflict: Ranges differ: 45–75 web.dev, 50–75 Kennedy, 60–80 Schöndorfer, 45–90 Butterick/USWDS

rules.rule: On mobile, keep the text column about 20–25 rem, giving 40–50 characters per line.
Keep multi-column text at 40–50 characters per line.
When you cannot count, check that two to three lowercase alphabets fit on one line.
Always use unitless line-height (e.g. 1.5), never px.
rules.why: Unitless values scale with font size.

rules.rule: Set long Latin body text at line-height 1.5–1.6; never leave the browser default of about 1.2.
rules.why: Browser default ~1.2 is too tight for body.
rules.conflict: Butterick print range 1.2–1.45 vs web sources 1.5+

rules.rule: Give longer lines more leading and shorter lines less.
Set mobile Latin body at line-height 1.3–1.45; Korean needs more.
Set headings and 1–2-line text at line-height 1.0–1.35 and test multi-line headings for colliding ascenders and descenders.
Set UI text, nav and notifications at line-height 1.2–1.3; buttons can use 1.0.
Do not set body text loose (e.g. 2.0).
rules.values: e.g. 2.0 too loose; 170% looked too loose
rules.why: Lines lose cohesion.

rules.rule: Give faces that look large at a size more leading and small-looking faces less.
Reference Material size/line-height pairs when building tokens.
rules.values: display-l 57/64, headline-l 32/40, title-l 22/28, body-l 16/24, body-m 14/20, label-l 14/20 px

rules.rule: Avoid tight leading for three or more lines; use loose leading for long passages and tight only in constrained rows.
Keep line heights on a grid where practical.
Leave tracking at 0 on lowercase body text.
rules.why: Fonts are already spaced for text sizes.

rules.rule: Add 5–12% tracking to all caps and small caps.
rules.why: Caps-on-caps look cramped.

rules.rule: Very small text may be loosened slightly.
Tighten large Latin headlines slightly.
rules.values: −0.5% to −2%; USWDS −1/−2/−3 tokens; Kennedy ~−1%; Material display-large −0.25 px
rules.why: Big type looks over-spaced at default tracking.
rules.conflict: KRDS +1px on Korean display vs Latin tightening; Apple: do not override system tracking

rules.rule: Never track so wide that another letter would fit in the gap.
Put the letter-spacing inside the caps or label style itself so it travels with the style.
Avoid letter-spacing on right-aligned or justified line ends, and check backgrounds and outlines for the trailing space.
rules.why: Letter-spacing adds trailing space after the last character.

rules.rule: Keep kerning on everywhere.
Use two weights for most UI: regular and one heavier weight.
Avoid weights below 400 for UI and body text; de-emphasise with colour or size instead.
rules.why: Hard to read at small sizes.

rules.rule: Use Black or Heavy weights only at large display sizes.
Use semibold for section headers, not long passages.
Emphasise with bold or italic, never both; never underline bold; never bold whole paragraphs.
In sans-serif text, emphasise with bold rather than italic.
rules.why: Sans italics barely stand out.

rules.rule: Underline only links.
Avoid text-background highlight (except hover) and strikethrough as emphasis.
Build hierarchy from weight, size and colour together, not size alone.
rules.why: A larger light line can outrank a smaller bold one.

rules.rule: Use 2–3 text colours: near-black primary, mid-grey secondary, lighter-grey tertiary.
Keep running text neutral; reserve coloured text for links, actions, code and warnings.
On coloured backgrounds never use grey text; use white at reduced opacity or a tint of the background hue.
rules.why: Grey reads as dirty on colour.

rules.rule: Hover and selected states must not change size, case or weight; change colour, background, underline or shadow.
rules.why: Changing size or weight causes layout shift.

rules.rule: Let only the page title pop by more emphasis alone; pair other up-pops with a down-pop, e.g. bold but smaller.
Use all caps only for under one line (labels, short headers, captions); never for paragraphs.
rules.why: Caps are slower to read and get skipped.

rules.rule: Write headings in sentence case; avoid all-caps and title-case headings.
Uppercase labels and buttons may be set slightly smaller than lowercase text.
rules.why: Caps look heavier.

rules.rule: Left-align running text; do not justify on the web.
rules.why: Browser justification makes rivers.

rules.rule: Centre only short lines like titles; never centre text blocks; break centred multi-line titles at phrase points.
Separate web paragraphs by space, not indent and never both.
Make the space above a heading at least 1.5x the space below it.
rules.why: Ties the heading to its own section.

rules.rule: Space list items at least 0.5 em apart.
Use at most one lead paragraph per page.
Use text-wrap: balance with a max width on headings and short quotes; never on body or on *.
rules.why: Prevents a one-word last line; costly on long text.

rules.rule: Use tabular figures for tables, prices, live values, timers and stacked numbers; proportional figures in prose.
rules.why: Aligned digits do not jitter.

rules.rule: Use lining figures with caps and in UI; oldstyle only in lowercase prose, never beside capitals.
Test for tabular figures by setting 0000 above 1111; equal widths mean tabular.
Turn on the case feature (case-sensitive punctuation) for all-caps labels where the font has it.
Use real typographic marks: curly quotes, …, ©/™, proper dashes, one space after full stops.
Make large UI symbols (%, +/−, arrows) larger and more spaced than text defaults where needed.
rules.why: Toss redrew them almost as icons.

rules.rule: Make layout survive user text-spacing overrides without clipping or overlap.
rules.values: line-height 1.5x, paragraph 2x, letter 0.12x, word 0.16x font size

rules.rule: Support OS and browser text scaling: allow multi-line labels and avoid forced one-line truncation.
rules.why: One-line ellipsis hid information at large text sizes.

rules.rule: Meet text contrast of 4.5:1 for normal and 3:1 for large text.
rules.values: 4.5:1 normal; 3:1 large (>= 24 px or >= 18.66 px bold); AAA 7:1 / 4.5:1

rules.rule: Serve fonts as WOFF2, preload critical files, limit file count and consider one variable font.
rules.why: Each file costs load time.

rules.rule: Use font-display with a short block and size-adjust on the fallback @font-face.
rules.why: Reduces layout shift.

rules.rule: Load every weight the tokens reference.
rules.why: Missing weights get faked.

rules.rule: Use a gothic (sans) Korean face for body and UI; non-gothic display faces only in banners.
rules.values: KRDS: Pretendard GOV; alt Noto Sans KR, Nanum Gothic, Spoqa Han Sans

rules.rule: Use Pretendard as a cross-platform system-ui substitute; its vertical metrics match SF.
rules.why: Layouts built on -apple-system behave the same.

rules.rule: Ship Korean webfonts as subsets or dynamic subsets.
rules.why: Only glyphs on the page get loaded.

rules.rule: Match Korean and Latin in one line by overall weight (grey value) and contrast, not one stroke measure.
Check a mixed sample like 「2026년 3월 Pro 요금제 9,900원」 at body size for thin or small Latin and digits.
rules.why: Ordinary Korean fonts make Latin and digits look smaller.

rules.rule: When pairing a separate Latin face with a Korean face, prefer a Latin face with a large x-height.
rules.why: Reduces the size gap with Hangul.

rules.rule: Prefer a Korean font with harmonised bundled Latin (Pretendard, Spoqa Han Sans, Toss Product Sans) over fallback mixing.
rules.why: Latin's visual centre sits lower than Hangul's.

rules.rule: If Japanese kana or kanji also appear, use a CJK face reduced for mixing.
Tune word spacing per script so readers do not notice the Korean/Latin difference.
rules.why: Korean fonts often have wider word spaces.

rules.rule: Check vertical centring of Korean text in buttons and chips on Windows, Android, iOS, Chrome and Safari.
rules.why: Toss had to retune vertical metrics.

rules.rule: Keep Korean body at 16 px minimum; with Pretendard GOV default to 17 px.
rules.values: min 16 px; 17 px with Pretendard GOV
rules.why: Pretendard GOV looks smaller than other faces at a size.

rules.rule: Use the KRDS size ladder for government-style Korean pages; body 400, headings 700.
Give Korean text at least 150% line height.
rules.why: Dense square Hangul needs more leading (inference).

rules.rule: Reference Toss TDS: 1.5 for body and about 1.33–1.45 for headings.
KLREQ gives 160% of character size as example leading for Korean text.
Set Korean body at 1.5–1.7, headings 1.3–1.4, one-line labels 1.2–1.4; never the Latin print range.
Keep Korean heading-to-body ratio about 1.25–1.5x.
Make in-app web pages follow the app's text-size scaling.
rules.why: Otherwise body text looks relatively small.

rules.rule: Start Korean body tracking at 0; tighten display only after a visual check, never below −0.02 em on body.
rules.values: 0 (KRDS body, headings below xl); body floor −0.02 em (inference)
rules.conflict: Korean blogs tighten Hangul −0.01 to −0.03em (unverified); Pretendard author avoided size tracking

rules.rule: On government-style pages, follow KRDS +1 px tracking on display and heading xl/l.
rules.conflict: KRDS +1px on Korean display vs Latin tightening; Apple: do not override system tracking

rules.rule: Choose per paragraph or document whether Korean breaks by syllable or by eojeol.
rules.why: KLREQ allows both.

rules.rule: Apply word-break: keep-all to short Korean text: titles, headings, buttons, labels, ad copy and UI.
rules.why: Words split mid-word look broken in big type.

rules.rule: On long Korean body use keep-all only with short-medium lines plus overflow-wrap: anywhere as a safety net.
rules.why: Syllable breaking is the traditional body norm.
rules.conflict: Shin: no keep-all on long body; many Korean product sites apply keep-all to body anyway

rules.rule: With keep-all on narrow elements, check for overflow from long words or URLs.
Combine text-wrap: balance with keep-all on Korean headings for even lines.
Follow Korean line-start/end bans; keep number+unit pairs together with   or nowrap.
rules.values: line-start bans: ) ? ! · . , -; line-end ban: opening brackets

rules.rule: Left-align Korean web body instead of justifying.
rules.why: Browsers justify Korean poorly.

rules.rule: Use no first-line indent for Korean web paragraphs.
In horizontal Korean, use half-width , and . and curly quotes “ ” ‘ ’.
rules.why: 「」『』 are traditional for vertical text.

rules.rule: Do not end Korean headings, titles or slogans with a full stop.
Join set items with a middle dot · and no spaces around it.
Attach a colon to the preceding word with a space after; no spaces in times, scores or chapter:verse.
Write ranges with a tilde and no spaces.
Use slashes without spaces by default; spaces allowed when paired phrases are multi-word.
Mark book titles with 『 』 or ≪ ≫ and chapters, artworks, laws, companies with 「 」 or < >.
Attach the opening quote to the following word and the closing quote to the preceding word.
Use …… as the standard Korean ellipsis, followed by a sentence mark at sentence end.
rules.values: Pretendard ss05 for a Korean-matched ellipsis; … / ... acceptance unverified

rules.rule: Emphasise Korean web text with bold; avoid italic on Hangul.
rules.why: Korean fonts have no true italic; browsers fake oblique.

rules.rule: Space a symbol or math sign about 1/8 em from adjacent Hangul; no extra space next to digits or Latin.
Flag Arial, Times New Roman or an unconsidered default face carrying the brand.
Flag a novelty or theme-acting font (handwriting, techy, spooky) in body or nav.
Flag two near-identical families paired, or three or more families on one page.
rules.conflict: Kennedy: ~95% of good pairs are serif+sans (S4); Butterick: similar faces often pair better (S1)

rules.rule: Flag thin or light weights (<= 300) on body or small UI text, especially light grey on white.
Flag hierarchy made by size alone, with every heading huge and no weight or colour steps.
Flag grey text on a coloured or photo background.
Flag pure black text with no secondary or tertiary colours, or decorative coloured body text.
Flag all-caps paragraphs, long all-caps buttons, untracked caps, or wide-tracked lowercase body.
Flag centred multi-line paragraphs such as hero subtitle blocks and feature descriptions.
Flag justified web text with rivers.
Flag desktop body lines running the full container width.
Flag px line-height, browser-default ~1.2 on body, or Korean body below 1.5.
Flag bold+italic together, underlined non-links, bold whole paragraphs, or italic emphasis in sans text.
Flag hover states that change weight or size and make text jump.
Flag straight quotes, ... from three periods, -- for dashes, and (c) for ©.
Flag proportional digits that wiggle in price tables, timers or stats.
Flag plain text on a busy photo with no overlay, floor fade, blur or scrim.
Flag headings with a one-word last line, and Korean headings split mid-word.
rules.why: Missing text-wrap: balance / keep-all.

rules.rule: Flag fixed-px-only text sizes that break OS scaling or truncate labels with ellipses.
Flag too many distinct sizes instead of a scale of about four roles.
rules.values: 7+ sizes on a simple landing page

rules.rule: Flag expressive display type inside cards, tables or form panels.
Flag Latin or digits visibly smaller or thinner than Hangul, and text off-centre in buttons.
rules.why: Fallback-font mixing.

rules.rule: Flag Korean headings ending with a full stop, spaced ranges like 「3 ~ 5일」, or a space before a colon.
Start from generous space and add elements into it; if a screen feels cramped, roughly double gaps before changing anything else.
rules.values: roughly 2× line, element and group gaps
rules.why: Default HTML starts at zero spacing and reads cramped; space alone looks intentional.

rules.rule: Group with space first; add dividers or background fills only when space alone is not enough.
rules.why: Space groups without adding elements; dividers and fills add clutter.
rules.conflict: Borders: RUI/Kennedy want space (S7,S6); NN/g wants a visible border/fill on clickable cards (S27,S30)

rules.rule: Keep gaps inside a group smaller than gaps between groups: label-to-field < field-to-field < section-to-section.
rules.why: People read close items as related (proximity).

rules.rule: Use one spacing scale as tokens and only its steps; no arbitrary values.
rules.why: Arbitrary values break rhythm and pull attention from the focus.

rules.rule: Shrink large spacing steps on small screens and keep small steps fixed.
rules.values: GOV.UK steps 0–3 (≤15px) fixed; step 9 60px desktop / 40px mobile; switch at 640px
rules.why: Big desktop gaps waste a phone screen; small inner gaps must stay readable.

rules.rule: Tie the base vertical gap between stacked blocks to body line-height and use multiples for larger gaps.
rules.why: One line of text is the natural unit of a text-heavy page.

rules.rule: Put spacing on the parent between siblings (stack, `* + *`), not on each child; push a card's footer action down with an auto margin.
rules.why: Margin is a relationship between neighbours; avoids doubled padding.

rules.rule: On Korean public-style sites, follow KRDS spacing values for header, breadcrumb, H1, footer, card lists and form stacks.
rules.values: header→breadcrumb 24; breadcrumb→H1 32–40; content→footer 40–64; card gap 24; inputs 16–24; label/helper stack 8; input padding 16; radio vert 16–24, horiz ≥24 px
rules.why: Official values Korean users meet on government sites.

rules.rule: Make a text box's inner padding equal on all four sides, measured from the x-height, not the line box.
rules.why: Line boxes add invisible space above caps; x-height centring looks centred.

rules.rule: Give an image inside a box a margin of at least half its shorter side.
rules.why: Smaller margins make the image feel jammed against the frame.

rules.rule: For nested rounded boxes set inner radius = outer radius − gap, never the same radius.
rules.why: Same radius on both gives an uneven band.

rules.rule: Give each view one dominant element and at most three levels of emphasis: dominant, sub-dominant, subordinate.
rules.why: People tell apart about three levels; two dominant items compete.

rules.rule: Use no more than three type sizes in a block and at most two large elements on a screen.
rules.why: More sizes flatten hierarchy.

rules.rule: Keep ordinary UI text (body, nav, buttons, captions) within about 2pt of each other; only headings break out.
rules.why: Wide size scatter reads as inconsistent.

rules.rule: Make only the page title fully loud; every other element mixes loud and quiet properties.
rules.why: Stacking all emphasis everywhere removes contrast.

rules.rule: De-emphasise with size, weight, contrast, case, tracking or margin; never with underline, background highlight or strikethrough.
rules.why: Underline reads as a link; highlight and strike carry other meanings.

rules.rule: Change colour, background, shadow or a small offset on hover/selected, never size, weight or case.
rules.why: Size or weight changes shift layout.

rules.rule: Run the squint/blur test with real photos in place; the intended order must still show.
rules.why: Strong imagery can override intended hierarchy.

rules.rule: Order content by importance top to bottom and leading to trailing; indent to show subordination.
rules.why: Matches reading order.

rules.rule: Design in greyscale first, then add one accent colour.
rules.values: simple designs: max 2 primary + 2 secondary colours
rules.why: Forces hierarchy from size, space and layout, not colour.

rules.rule: Align to as few edges as possible; ragged right edges of left-aligned text do not count as an edge.
rules.why: Fewer, stronger edges look tidy.

rules.rule: Hang bullets, icons and opening quote marks outside the text's left edge.
rules.why: Keeps the text edge clean.

rules.rule: Left-align body text and keep main lines at 8–12 words, sidebars and captions at 5–6.
rules.why: Comfortable reading; justified text needs hand tuning.
rules.conflict: Measure: 60ch (S16) vs ~75 chars (S20) vs 8–12 words (S32); Korean cap ~35–40 syllables (inference)

rules.rule: Centre polygon icons (play, star) on their circumscribed circle, not their bounding box.
rules.why: Optical centre differs from geometric centre.

rules.rule: Place a control on the thing it changes, list-wide controls above the list, and the primary form action at the end of the form flow.
rules.why: Users look for controls near the object; distant controls must stand out more.

rules.rule: Vary section layouts by one simple rule (e.g. alternate image left/right) and mark section starts/ends with a repeated element.
rules.why: Gives rhythm without chaos.

rules.rule: Cap reading width in `ch`, not px.
rules.why: Long lines tire readers; ch scales with font size.
rules.conflict: Measure: 60ch (S16) vs ~75 chars (S20) vs 8–12 words (S32); Korean cap ~35–40 syllables (inference)

rules.rule: Cap page content width so wide screens do not stretch lines and gaps.
rules.values: GOV.UK 1020px; KRDS 1200px with 24px side margins (1200 from 1248px viewport)
rules.why: Wide screens otherwise stretch lines and gaps.

rules.rule: Put main reading content in a two-thirds column; use standard splits.
rules.why: Keeps measure in range while leaving a side column.

rules.rule: On Korean sites use the KRDS grid, keep gutter ≤ half a column, and never mix column counts on one screen.
rules.why: Official Korean grid; edge margins prevent mis-taps.
rules.conflict: Breakpoints: named sets (GOV.UK, KRDS, Material) vs intrinsic/container-driven (Every Layout, web.dev)

rules.rule: Use percentage columns, not fixed pixel widths or heights.
rules.why: Fixed sizes break responsive layout.

rules.rule: Build mobile first: single column in source order, confirm the order makes sense, then widen.
rules.why: Small screens use the source order.
rules.conflict: Desktop effort: Baemin draws mobile only, QAs desktop after build (S37); Android optimises expanded (S25)

rules.rule: Set breakpoints where the content breaks, not at device widths, and use `em` in media queries.
rules.values: e.g. two columns from 45em; two text columns only beyond ~50em
rules.why: Device sizes change every year.
rules.conflict: Breakpoints: named sets (GOV.UK, KRDS, Material) vs intrinsic/container-driven (Every Layout, web.dev)

rules.rule: Prefer intrinsic layouts that need no media query, such as auto-fill card grids and wrapping sidebars.
rules.values: grid repeat(auto-fill, minmax(15em, 1fr)), gap 1em; sidebar wraps when main <50% width
rules.why: Fewer breakpoints; works in any container.
rules.conflict: Breakpoints: named sets (GOV.UK, KRDS, Material) vs intrinsic/container-driven (Every Layout, web.dev)

rules.rule: Make components respond to their container (container queries) and pages to the viewport.
rules.values: e.g. media object stacks below 25em container width
rules.why: The same card may sit in a wide column or a narrow sidebar.
rules.conflict: Breakpoints: named sets (GOV.UK, KRDS, Material) vs intrinsic/container-driven (Every Layout, web.dev)

rules.rule: If you need named breakpoints, use Material widths or KRDS widths for Korean sites.
rules.values: Material compact <600, medium 600–839, expanded 840–1199, large 1200–1599, XL ≥1600; KRDS 360/768/1024/1280/1440
rules.why: Covers >93% of devices per class.
rules.conflict: Breakpoints: named sets (GOV.UK, KRDS, Material) vs intrinsic/container-driven (Every Layout, web.dev)

rules.rule: Keep the same functions at every size and change only how much is shown; test smallest, largest and largest-text first.
rules.why: Users switch devices; extremes reveal clipping.

rules.rule: Let text grow: support zoom and large text, stack side-by-side items when text is large, set min/max widths in relative units.
rules.values: Toss: many labels ≥5 chars; menu widths as % of screen
rules.why: Korean labels and enlarged text overflow fixed widths.

rules.rule: Do not infer touch from width; enlarge targets under `pointer: coarse` and never shrink them for fine pointers.
rules.why: Fitts's law applies to everyone.

rules.rule: Never put essential content or controls behind hover; any hover reveal must also open on focus.
rules.why: Touch users cannot hover; keyboard users need parity.
rules.conflict: Hover reveal: Kennedy accepts per-item hover actions (S5); web.dev and NN/g warn against it (S14,S29)

rules.rule: For Toss-style mobile pages, design at 360–420px (base 375px) and test on 3–5 real devices incl. one small and one large safe area.
rules.why: Covers 70–80% of Toss traffic.

rules.rule: Use photos that carry information (the actual product, shop, food, staff, place); skip generic stock and feel-good filler.
rules.values: real staff photos ~10% more viewing time than 3× larger bios; generic thumbnails 18% of viewing time
rules.why: Eyetracking: users ignore decorative stock.

rules.rule: Show detailed, specific product photos with alternate views, and enlargements at least 2× the default size.
rules.why: Users study detail when they choose a product.

rules.rule: Keep one primary graphic per screen and make others small icons; never let graphics cover key information or force scrolling.
rules.why: Competing graphics outweigh text and CTA.

rules.rule: Never set plain text on an uncontrolled photo; use a dark overlay, a semi-opaque box, blur or a bottom fade, with white text.
rules.why: Photos change and crop at different widths.

rules.rule: Give every image width/height or aspect-ratio, object-fit: cover with a set object-position, and max-inline-size: 100%.
rules.why: Prevents layout jump and squashed photos.

rules.rule: Lazy-load below-the-fold images; load the hero eagerly and give only the LCP image fetchpriority=high.
rules.why: Improves perceived speed.

rules.rule: Give every image alt text, decorative ones alt="", and prefer CSS for purely decorative imagery.
rules.why: Screen readers need it.

rules.rule: Scale background art to fill and never distort its aspect ratio.
rules.why: Distorted art looks broken.

rules.rule: Pair icons with visible text labels, except a few universal ones (home, search magnifier, print).
rules.why: Most icons are ambiguous; an obscure icon is a wasted feature.

rules.rule: If no fitting icon turns up in about 5 seconds, use a word instead.
rules.why: The concept probably has no clear icon.

rules.rule: Keep one meaning per icon across the whole site.
rules.why: Inconsistent icons cannot be learned.

rules.rule: Match icon stroke weight to adjacent text weight and icon corner radius to the font's corners.
rules.why: Icon and text read as one unit.

rules.rule: Size icons relative to text (≈1em) and scale them with text size; keep the hamburger icon small.
rules.why: Oversized icons shout; fixed icons break under large text.

rules.rule: Never stack two icons, or an icon and an emoji, on one item.
rules.why: Visual noise.

rules.rule: Use inline SVG icons; mark decorative ones aria-hidden and give icon-only buttons an accessible name.
rules.why: Screen readers need names, not shapes.

rules.rule: On desktop show navigation as text links instead of hiding it behind an icon.
rules.why: Icons that stand out on phones get lost on large screens.

rules.rule: Use one light source from above (slightly left): raised items cast shadows, recessed ones (inputs, tracks, checkboxes) look inset.
rules.why: Mixed light directions look like blurry borders, not depth.
rules.conflict: Flat vs depth: Toss near-flat with blur/outline (S34); NN/g and Kennedy keep depth cues (S30,S1)

rules.rule: Make all shadows share one x:y ratio and grow together, defined as three named elevation tokens.
rules.values: y = 2x; higher = larger offset, larger blur, lower opacity; 3 levels (small, medium, large)
rules.why: Consistency reads as a coherent space.

rules.rule: Tint shadows with the background hue instead of pure black, layering several low-opacity shadows; do not animate them.
rules.values: e.g. 5 layers at 0.075; fewer layers on low-end phones
rules.why: Black shadows grey out coloured backgrounds.
rules.conflict: Shadow colour: Kennedy uses translucent black (S3); Comeau wants hue-tinted (S8); tint on coloured bg

rules.rule: Scale shadow and border strength with the background luminance of the element.
rules.values: mid-tone: 0 1px 2px 30% black, 1px border ~20% black; dark: 0 2px 4px 50%, border ~50%
rules.why: The same shadow looks wrong on different luminances.
rules.conflict: Shadow colour: Kennedy uses translucent black (S3); Comeau wants hue-tinted (S8); tint on coloured bg

rules.rule: Keep clickable things with at least one cue (fill, shadow, contrasting colour, underline); go flat only at low density with high-contrast actions.
rules.values: weak signifiers: 22% longer to find, 25% more fixations
rules.why: Ghost buttons and text-styled links were missed in eyetracking.
rules.conflict: Flat vs depth: Toss near-flat with blur/outline (S34); NN/g and Kennedy keep depth cues (S30,S1)

rules.rule: Use fewer borders; replace them with a shadow, a background contrast or more space.
rules.why: Many borders make a design busy.
rules.conflict: Borders: RUI/Kennedy want space (S7,S6); NN/g wants a visible border/fill on clickable cards (S27,S30)

rules.rule: Lighten overlays and popups with background blur plus a thin bright outline instead of a heavy dark scrim.
rules.why: Toss uses this to reduce visual weight.
rules.conflict: Flat vs depth: Toss near-flat with blur/outline (S34); NN/g and Kennedy keep depth cues (S30,S1)

rules.rule: Use one primary (filled) button per view and make supporting actions secondary.
rules.why: Several primaries compete and hide the next step.

rules.rule: Label buttons with the specific action in sentence case ("저장하고 계속", "주소 추가") and do not repeat on-screen text in the CTA.
rules.why: Says what happens next.

rules.rule: Align the primary button to the form's left edge, inside the flow.
rules.why: Users finish forms there.

rules.rule: Avoid disabled buttons and show why instead; destructive actions get a warning style only with confirmation and explanatory text.
rules.why: Disabled buttons have poor contrast and confuse.

rules.rule: Size the baseline button with proper padding, touch targets at least 44×44pt, and larger padding under pointer: coarse.
rules.values: 40px tall, 20px horizontal padding at 16px text; ≥44×44pt; coarse e.g. 1em 2em
rules.why: Default proportions and finger accuracy.

rules.rule: Match button radius, letter-spacing and shape to the typeface: rounded font small radius, squared font square corners, caps labels tracked.
rules.why: Deliberate choices instead of defaults.

rules.rule: Prevent double submit and show progress while waiting.
rules.why: Slow connections cause duplicate sends.

rules.rule: Give touch feedback, such as a one-step darker background or haptic.
rules.why: Confirms the tap registered.

rules.rule: On mobile prefer large row-style choices over tiny round radios, and make the selection count clear from the question text.
rules.values: Toss test: 13/15 chose correctly regardless of control shape
rules.why: Small circles are poor finger targets; context matters more.

rules.rule: Use cards for browsing mixed content, a list for similar items to compare (prices, schedules), and a plain grid for photo galleries.
rules.why: Cards are less scannable and harder to compare.

rules.rule: Build a card as one container (image → title → short summary → action), fixed width, content height, whole card as link, secondary actions apart.
rules.why: Bigger target and clear information scent.

rules.rule: Signal a card with a border or contrasting background, optionally a slight shadow.
rules.why: Signals grouping and clickability.
rules.conflict: Borders: RUI/Kennedy want space (S7,S6); NN/g wants a visible border/fill on clickable cards (S27,S30)

rules.rule: Keep the same internal layout across cards in one set.
rules.why: Users compare cards back and forth.

rules.rule: Show "-" for missing values in structured lists and keep toolbars in a fixed position and order.
rules.why: Predictable structure on public data pages.

rules.rule: Replace every default (font, colour, radius, shadow, spacing) with a deliberate choice; avoid the plain blue 40px button.
rules.why: Defaults chosen by nobody look templated.

rules.rule: Design for this business's content and tasks, not to look good as a static picture; avoid surface polish that makes products converge.
rules.why: Styles converge so unrelated products look alike.

rules.rule: Replace generic stock and decorative filler images with the real staff, shop or product.
rules.why: Users ignore stock photos.

rules.rule: Remove decorative effects with no information: particles, heavy gradients, decorative illustrations, several hero graphics, needless error/loading art.
rules.why: Decoration without meaning signals a template.

rules.rule: Check depth consistency: no mixed shadow angles or offset ratios, no pure-black shadows on colour, no glow-like shadows.
rules.why: Inconsistent depth looks generated.
rules.conflict: Shadow colour: Kennedy uses translucent black (S3); Comeau wants hue-tinted (S8); tint on coloured bg

rules.rule: Flag pages where everything is emphasised: many sizes, more than two large elements, all bold, accent on everything, no dominant element.
rules.why: Equal emphasis leaves no focal point.

rules.rule: Flag font-size scatter among ordinary elements beyond ~2pt or more than three sizes in one block.
rules.why: Size scatter reads as inconsistent.

rules.rule: Flag irregular off-scale gaps, and uniform gaps that ignore grouping (same space inside and between groups).
rules.why: Gaps must follow scale and grouping.

rules.rule: Flag borders and dividers everywhere where space would do.
rules.why: Borders everywhere look busy and templated.
rules.conflict: Borders: RUI/Kennedy want space (S7,S6); NN/g wants a visible border/fill on clickable cards (S27,S30)

rules.rule: Flag cards used for everything, including uniform lists and galleries, out of habit.
rules.why: "Cards look modern" is not a reason.

rules.rule: Flag ghost buttons and text-styled links used as primary actions.
rules.why: Flat to the point of no signifier.
rules.conflict: Flat vs depth: Toss near-flat with blur/outline (S34); NN/g and Kennedy keep depth cues (S30,S1)

rules.rule: Flag several primary buttons competing, and CTA text that repeats the heading.
rules.why: Competing CTAs hide the next step.

rules.rule: Flag icons without labels, invented icons, icon + emoji stacks and oversized hamburger icons.
rules.why: Ambiguous or decorative icons look generated.

rules.rule: Flag fixed pixel widths/heights that break under long Korean labels or large text.
rules.why: Korean labels and enlarged text overflow.

rules.rule: Flag text dropped straight on a photo with no overlay, which fails on some crops.
rules.why: Crops change per width.

rules.rule: Study the best work for its reasoning, but do not copy a popular showcase look without its context.
rules.why: Copying the surface without the problem produces sameness.
rules.conflict: Kennedy recommends studying the best work (S2); Adams warns copying the surface breeds sameness (S33)

rules.rule: Avoid the convergent AI-site look: Inter, indigo/purple gradient, centred hero, three rounded cards with large shadow.
rules.why: Reported as the common AI-built look (secondhand; original not read).
rules.by: secondhand commentary (Adam Wathan post, not read)

rules.rule: Give every action visible feedback at once: a pressed state, then the result.
rules.why: Silent actions get repeated.

rules.rule: Use the customer's words in labels and menus, not internal or industry jargon.
rules.why: Matching the real world lowers learning cost.

rules.rule: Give every flow a visible exit (Cancel / Back) and, where possible, Undo.
rules.why: Prevents lock-in after a mis-tap.

rules.rule: Give the same thing the same name and the same position everywhere, following conventions from other sites.
rules.why: Consistency; Jakob's Law.

rules.rule: Prevent errors first with constraints, sensible defaults and disabled impossible choices.
rules.why: Cheaper than recovering.

rules.rule: Keep options and labels visible instead of making users remember them.
rules.why: Recognition beats recall.

rules.rule: Remove any element that does not serve the page's main task.
rules.why: Extra elements compete with the important ones.

rules.rule: Keep help short, contextual, task-focused and placed where the question arises.
rules.why: Users skip manuals (Paradox of the Active User).

rules.rule: Make primary buttons large and close to where the eye or thumb already is.
rules.why: Fitts's Law: hit time grows with distance, shrinks with size.

rules.rule: Limit choices per decision point and group long lists into chunks.
rules.why: Hick's Law, choice overload, chunking.

rules.rule: Use standard layouts: logo top-left, nav in the header, cart top-right, utilities in the footer.
rules.why: Jakob's Law: users expect your site to work like others.

rules.rule: Group related items by proximity and shared containers; separate unrelated ones with space.
rules.why: Proximity and common region.

rules.rule: Make only one thing visually distinct per area: the primary CTA.
rules.why: Von Restorff: if everything stands out nothing does.

rules.rule: Put the most important items first and last in lists and menus.
rules.why: Serial position effect.

rules.rule: Keep interface responses under ~0.4 s where possible and under 0.1 s for direct manipulation.
rules.values: <0.4 s; <0.1 s direct manipulation; 0.1/1/10 s limits
rules.why: Doherty threshold; response-time limits.

rules.rule: Show progress in multi-step flows (step x of y) and end with a clear confirmation.
rules.why: Goal-gradient, peak-end, Zeigarnik.
rules.conflict: W3C/KRDS: show progress in multi-step forms; GOV.UK: only if research shows need

rules.rule: Absorb unavoidable complexity in the system with auto-fill and auto-format, and accept input liberally.
rules.why: Tesler's Law; Postel's Law.

rules.rule: On desktop, show the primary navigation; never hide it behind a hamburger.
rules.values: hidden nav used 27% vs 48–50% visible; discoverability fell >20%
rules.why: Hidden navigation is used far less.

rules.rule: On mobile, show up to 4 top-level items visibly; beyond that use a menu plus in-page links.
rules.values: ≤4 visible items; combo nav used 86% vs 57% hidden
rules.why: Visible combo nav gets used more.

rules.rule: Mark the current location with a highlighted menu item or a breadcrumb.
rules.why: Visibility of status.

rules.rule: Make menu labels specific, familiar and front-loaded; icons only support text, never replace it.
rules.why: Vague or invented labels kill information scent.

rules.rule: Open submenus on click/tap, not hover only, and mark them with a caret.
rules.why: Hover fails on touch and keyboard.

rules.rule: Avoid multi-level cascading menus; use mega menus or landing pages instead.
rules.why: Cascades are hard to steer.

rules.rule: Breadcrumbs show hierarchy, not history, end with the unlinked current page, and are skipped on sites 1–2 levels deep.
On mobile, shorten breadcrumbs to the parent level and do not let them wrap.
Footer carries contact, customer service, privacy policy and terms; repeat main nav on long pages, ~2 levels.
rules.why: Users look for these there.

rules.rule: Use infinite scroll only for browse feeds; shops and search results get pagination or Load more.
rules.why: Keeps the footer reachable and items findable again.

rules.rule: Links navigate, buttons act; checkout steps are the accepted exception.
rules.why: Links support new tabs and visited state.

rules.rule: In the first screen, state who you are and what you offer: name, logo top-left, one concrete tagline.
rules.why: Generic Welcome lines waste the most-read space.

rules.rule: Use real photos of the actual business, product, staff and process, not stock decoration.
rules.why: Real imagery informs and builds credibility.

rules.rule: Show concrete content examples (products, menu items, services with prices), not only category links.
Avoid false floors: make it obvious the page continues below the first screen.
Give the page one visually dominant primary task and group secondary paths by audience.
No autoplay video, animated headline or logo, splash screens or non-legal popups.
rules.why: Motion distracts and delays core content.

rules.rule: Prefer one static hero over a carousel; if used: ≤5 frames, position count, controls, no mobile auto-advance.
rules.why: Many users never see later frames.

rules.rule: Front-load key facts in the first two paragraphs and headings' first two words; lists for lists; bold sparingly.
rules.values: first two paragraphs; first two words
rules.why: Users scan in F-patterns.

rules.rule: Ask only what you need; justify every field and drop the rest.
rules.why: Each field adds abandonment.

rules.rule: Use a single-column form; only tightly related short fields share a row (city/postcode, start/end date).
rules.why: Keeps vertical flow.

rules.rule: Put labels above fields and keep them always visible; never replace them with placeholders.
rules.why: Placeholders vanish and hurt review, contrast, screen readers.
rules.conflict: NN/g: floating labels only when space is tight; label above stays best

rules.rule: Put hints and format rules outside the field, before input, in one short sentence.
Size inputs to the expected length and show units next to the field, not inside the label.
For 2–5 options use radio or segmented buttons, a stepper for small counts; dropdowns only for long lists.
rules.why: Dropdowns hide options and cost extra taps.

rules.rule: Use one full-name field instead of a first/last split; this is also the Korean convention.
rules.values: 42% typed full name into First name
rules.why: Split name fields confuse users.

rules.rule: Hide rarely needed fields (address line 2, company, coupon) behind a link.
rules.why: Visible coupon fields send users off-site hunting codes.

rules.rule: Explain why sensitive data (phone, ID) is needed, right next to the field.
rules.values: 68% reluctant to give phone at checkout
rules.why: Users hesitate to share personal data.

rules.rule: Use correct input types and autocomplete attributes so mobile keyboards and autofill work.
Never block paste, and offer show password.
Ask each piece of information once per journey; pre-fill from earlier steps or the logged-in profile.
No Reset/Clear buttons; if Cancel exists, make it visually weaker than Submit.
rules.why: Prevents accidental data loss.

rules.rule: Group radio sets with fieldset/legend and give every control a programmatic label.
Split long forms into steps with progress, allow going back without data loss, offer save-draft for long applications.
rules.conflict: W3C/KRDS: show progress in multi-step forms; GOV.UK: only if research shows need

rules.rule: Before final submit of a consequential form, show a check-your-answers summary with a change link per section.
rules.why: Catches mistakes and raises confidence.

rules.rule: Avoid time limits; if unavoidable, warn in advance with extend and log out buttons.
Use one primary (filled) button per view and at most two prominent buttons.
rules.why: Hierarchy guides the next step.
rules.conflict: GOV.UK: Continue left; KRDS: bottom-right, submit rightmost; Apple: full-width on small screens

rules.rule: Start button labels with a verb naming the outcome (예약하기, 장바구니 담기), about four words or fewer.
rules.why: Users scan buttons and read only the first words.

rules.rule: Replace Learn more / Click here with destination-specific text; every link label unique out of context.
rules.why: Information scent; screen-reader link lists.

rules.rule: Show progress inside the button (spinner, 결제 중…) and block duplicate submission; still dedupe on the server.
rules.why: Users re-click when nothing seems to happen.
rules.conflict: GOV.UK: avoid disabled submit; KRDS: may disable until required fields filled

rules.rule: Never make destructive actions the default; two steps, warning style only on the final confirm, not red alone.
Highlight the preferred option by style, not size; keep button sizes equal within a set.
Make touch targets 44×44 pt/CSS px; never below 24×24 CSS px without spacing.
rules.why: Finger width limits density.

rules.rule: Give every custom button a visible pressed state and a visible keyboard focus state.
On mobile keep a high content-to-chrome ratio; each new element must justify what it pushes off-screen.
On mobile, lead with the gist and show details on demand.
Save state continuously so interrupted users can resume.
rules.why: Mobile sessions are fragmented.

rules.rule: Make tasks self-contained; do not require copying data between apps.
Use device capabilities to cut typing: location, camera, biometrics, wallet pay, tel links for 전화하기.
Give every gesture a visible on-screen button alternative.
rules.why: Gestures are hard to discover.

rules.rule: Keep at least ~8 px between touch targets, more for frequent or costly actions.
Use +/- buttons with an editable field for quantities, not a bare text box.
rules.why: Mobile suffers most.

rules.rule: Show the full price incl. delivery, tax and fees on the product page and before payment details.
rules.why: Surprise costs drive abandonment.

rules.rule: Offer guest checkout and offer account creation after purchase.
Target 8–14 form elements in checkout.
rules.values: 8–14 elements; average ~23; most sites need ~8 fields

rules.rule: Default billing address to shipping and reveal billing fields only on demand.
Show an estimated delivery or pickup date or range, not only a speed like 2–3일.
rules.why: Users should not have to calculate.

rules.rule: Collapse completed checkout steps into readable summaries.
Mark both required and optional fields.
rules.values: 32% missed a required field when only optional was marked
rules.conflict: GOV.UK: mark only optional (선택); Baymard: mark both; KRDS: mark the minority site-wide

rules.rule: Product page: real photos with zoom, descriptive name, short front-loaded text, per-option stock, clear add-to-cart.
Make reviews sortable and filterable, negatives easy to find, with reviewer context and verified-purchase marks.
rules.why: Shoppers read negatives first.

rules.rule: Booking pickers: calendar within ~a year, typed entry beyond; grey out unavailable dates, block impossible ranges.
rules.why: Keep month view stable; highlight the selected range.

rules.rule: For a short list of available slots, show them as tappable buttons instead of a calendar.
Accept flexible formats (spaces, hyphens, leading zeros) and normalise them, e.g. 010 1234 5678.
rules.why: Postel's Law.

rules.rule: Ask eligibility questions first and tell people early if they cannot use the service.
After completion show a confirmation screen with a key-details summary, status link and next action.
Show phone, address and business hours prominently, at least in the header utility area and footer.
Disclose prices, fees, refund/return policy and delivery charges up front; link policies near the purchase action.
Fix typos, broken links and layout bugs before sending.
rules.why: They signal carelessness or even hacking.

rules.rule: Do not gate value behind login or personal-data walls.
Show the real process and the real people doing the work.
Link to third-party reviews and presence (maps, review sites, social).
rules.why: Trusted more than self-hosted testimonials.

rules.rule: Visually encapsulate card/payment fields with a distinct border or background and 1–2 security marks inside.
rules.values: 1–2 marks; 19% abandon for distrust of card handling
rules.why: Perceived security is a gut feeling.

rules.rule: Keep information accurate and current; if an update is delayed, say so and when it will be fixed.
Place each error next to its field, plus on submit a summary at the top that receives focus.
rules.conflict: GOV.UK: submit only; Baymard: inline on blur; KRDS: keyup/focus-out; NN/g: live only for passwords

rules.rule: Error text says what went wrong and how to fix it in plain words, reusing the field's label.
Never signal errors by colour only; combine icon, border, text and weight.
Keep the user's input after an error; never clear the field.
Do not show errors before the user has had a chance to type (no error on focus or empty blur).
rules.why: Feels like a false accusation.
rules.conflict: GOV.UK: submit only; Baymard: inline on blur; KRDS: keyup/focus-out; NN/g: live only for passwords

rules.rule: Clear the error as soon as the input becomes valid.
rules.conflict: GOV.UK: submit only; Baymard: inline on blur; KRDS: keyup/focus-out; NN/g: live only for passwords

rules.rule: Match severity to component: inline/toast for minor, dialog for severe; never put important errors in a vanishing toast.
Offer the fix as an action (retry, 문의하기, suggested correction) instead of instructions to phone someone.
Treat eligibility/permission problems as outcomes: send users to a page explaining the result and next step.
rules.why: They are not validation errors.

rules.rule: No humour, oops or blame words (잘못된, invalid, forbidden) in routine errors.
rules.conflict: NN/g allows delight only in total outages; Material/GOV.UK reject humour in errors; GOV.UK bans please/sorry in errors; Toss and KRDS require a polite style

rules.rule: Never show a blank empty state: say nothing is here yet, what will appear, and give a button to add the first item.
Never show no results while data is still loading.
rules.why: Destroys trust.

rules.rule: Loading: under 1 s show nothing; 1–10 s spinner or skeleton with text; over 10 s percent or steps, estimate and cancel.
rules.values: <1 s nothing; 1–10 s spinner/skeleton; >10 s percent-done + estimate + cancel

rules.rule: Make skeletons preview the actual layout, not just header and footer frames.
Confirm only serious irreversible actions; name item and effect; outcome-labelled buttons, no default on destroy; else Undo.
rules.why: Overused confirms get clicked blindly.

rules.rule: Keep text contrast at least 4.5:1 (3:1 for large/bold text) and focus indicators at least 3:1.
Keep focus visible everywhere; no outline:none without an equal replacement; never hide focus under sticky bars.
Focus order follows visual order; no positive tabindex; first focusable element is a 본문 바로가기 skip link.
Give the page a descriptive title, lang="ko" and a real heading hierarchy (form sections use h2–h6).
Give meaningful images short alt text describing their purpose.
Text must enlarge to 200% without breaking the layout.
Respect reduced-motion preferences; no autoplay audio or video without controls.
After an error, move focus to it or the first errored field; after a modal error closes, return focus to the field.
Give range sliders and drag-only controls a non-drag alternative.
Provide built-in text-size and high-contrast options for public or senior-heavy services.
Pick a tone on four axes, stay near the middle, and get more serious for errors, money and health.
Write so the next screen is predictable: the button or link says what happens after tapping.
Cut words that change nothing (앞으로, 해당; ~하실 수 있습니다 → ~할 수 있어요) and sentences repeating the title.
One message per sentence; it must sound natural when read aloud.
Suggest, do not threaten; no fear or loss framing to stop users leaving.
Use words anyone understands; no slang, memes or industry terms.
Frame copy around what users can do, not what they cannot.
Refer to controls by their label text, not their type (저장 버튼을 누르세요 → 저장을 누르세요).
A dialog's title and buttons alone should explain the decision.
Unify messages for the same situation and template recurring ones (maintenance: only bank/time vary).
Use sentence case for English UI on bilingual sites.
rules.why: Apple uses title case; irrelevant for Korean.

rules.rule: Validate format on blur, live only for password rules, and always re-check on submit with an error summary.
rules.why: Practical compromise across sources.
rules.conflict: GOV.UK: submit only; Baymard: inline on blur; KRDS: keyup/focus-out; NN/g: live only for passwords

rules.rule: Keep submit enabled and explain on press; disable it only while processing.
rules.why: Practical compromise across sources.
rules.conflict: GOV.UK: avoid disabled submit; KRDS: may disable until required fields filled

rules.rule: Korean mobile web: full-width bottom primary button; desktop public-service forms follow KRDS placement.
rules.why: Market norm in Korea.
rules.conflict: GOV.UK: Continue left; KRDS: bottom-right, submit rightmost; Apple: full-width on small screens

rules.rule: Carry politeness in the ending (해요체), skip ritual apologies except for real service failures.
rules.why: Politeness lives in the Korean ending, not filler.
rules.conflict: GOV.UK bans please/sorry in errors; Toss and KRDS require a polite style

rules.rule: Pick one speech level per product (해요체 for shops/booking) and record it; never mix 해요체 and 합니다체 on one screen.
rules.why: Toss uses 해요체 everywhere; KRDS asks a reassuring polite style.

rules.rule: Check every screen against Toss's 8 writing principles (predictable next screen, cut weeds, empty sentences, etc.).
Errors: prevent first, right component, a one-tap self-fix in user language, ~할 수 있어요 over commands.
Avoid 한자어 and admin words in consumer copy (해당, 상기, 기재, 금일, 익일 → 이, 위, 적기, 오늘, 다음 날).
rules.why: Read-aloud test.

rules.rule: Use one 이름 field; Korean users do not split family and given name.
Accept phone numbers with or without hyphens/spaces, auto-format, and use type="tel" autocomplete="tel".
Korean address: 도로명주소 postcode search → auto-filled base address → one 상세주소 field; no second line by default.
rules.why: Matches Baymard's address-lookup advice.

rules.rule: Login: same visible spot with icon+label, common methods untabbed, ID hints, show-password, find-ID links, 로그인 안 함.
Applications: official title, all channels, eligibility first, no tabs inside a step, temp save, confirm, status page.
Confirm dialogs only for hard-to-undo actions; action-named buttons (동의함/동의안함); say what refusing restricts.
Government sites show the official government banner and logo in header and footer.
Small businesses: add the footer business-info block (상호, 대표자, 사업자등록번호, 통신판매업 신고번호, 주소, 연락처).
rules.why: Korean legal/market convention; verify per business type.

rules.rule: For senior-heavy audiences (clinics, local services), offer text-size controls, large touch areas and adjustable contrast.
rules.why: KWCAG 2.2; Kakao guide.

rules.rule: Build a small glossary and message templates per project so the voice stays one person.
rules.why: Toss runs one voice across ~40 services.

rules.rule: Use verb-noun -하기 or plain-noun buttons (예약하기, 장바구니, 다음); use 확인 only when it truly confirms.
rules.why: Korean market norm; 다음 is the step-button convention.

rules.rule: Define fixed colour steps up front: 8–10 greys and 5–10 shades each for the primary and accent colours.
rules.why: Ad-hoc shades break the system; an unlimited palette is no system.

rules.rule: Build each scale from base 500 (button fill), then 900 for text and 100 for tints, then 700/300, then 800/600/400/200.
rules.why: Choosing the edges by use gives shades that work in real components.

rules.rule: Reference fixed colour tokens; never generate shades at runtime with lighten()/darken(), color-mix() or similar.
rules.why: Hand-tuned steps stay perceptually even; function output does not.

rules.rule: For darker variants lower brightness and raise saturation; for lighter variants raise brightness and lower saturation (HSB).
rules.why: A plain black overlay only drops brightness and looks muddy.

rules.rule: Optionally shift hue with lightness: darker shades toward 0/120/240°, lighter shades toward 60/180/300°.
rules.why: Keeps shades vivid instead of dull.
rules.conflict: Hue shift toward luminance extremes (Kennedy) vs fixed hue (Stripe, KRDS); Spectrum shifts a few only

rules.rule: Build colour scales in a perceptual space (CIELAB, LCH, OKLCH), not HSL lightness.
rules.why: Equal HSL lightness looks different per hue, so contrast is uneven.

rules.rule: Tune every hue so the same step number gives the same contrast across hues.
rules.values: Stripe: steps 5+ apart pass small text; 4+ apart pass icons and large text
rules.why: Contrast becomes checkable by step number.

rules.rule: Tie step names to contrast against the background end of the scale, KRDS style, and adjust the base until it passes.
rules.why: The step name alone tells whether a pair passes.

rules.rule: Give each scale step one role (Radix 12-step): app backgrounds, component states, borders, solid fill, then text.
rules.values: 1–2 app bg; 3/4/5 component bg default/hover/pressed; 6 subtle border; 7 interactive border; 8 strong border/focus; 9 solid; 10 solid hover; 11 low-contrast text; 12 high-contrast text; 11/12 reach APCA Lc 60/90 on step 2
rules.why: Each step has one job, so nothing is picked at random.

rules.rule: Put dark text on yellow, amber, lime and similar light solid fills; use white text on most other hues.
rules.why: Their solid steps are too light for white text.

rules.rule: Make the lightest tint of every hue safe as a text background, just like white.
rules.why: Text then works on highlighted sections without re-checking pairs.

rules.rule: Check the gamut instead of forcing physically impossible colours such as a very dark yellow.
Check that hues are distinguishable separately from contrast; contrast is not vibrancy.
rules.why: WCAG measures only luminance contrast.

rules.rule: Use palette values first; add a new colour only if it will be reused.
Design in greyscale first, then add colour last and only with a purpose.
rules.why: Forces hierarchy to come from spacing, size and weight.

rules.rule: Start from the simplest scheme that works: one accent on a greyscale base, or several shades of one hue.
Derive a customisable theme from very few inputs, such as base colour, accent colour and a contrast value.
rules.why: Few inputs give consistent themes and allow a high-contrast variant.

rules.rule: Start greys from a very dark grey, never pure black, and take the lightest grey from an off-white background.
Let neutrals dominate the page and use other colours sparingly.
rules.why: Carbon's default themes are mostly grey.

rules.rule: Tint neutrals toward the brand hue only lightly.
rules.values: Linear limited accent blue in its neutral calculation; KRDS uses blue-grey
rules.why: Looks more neutral and dates less.

rules.rule: Build surface hierarchy with background layer tokens, not ad-hoc fills.
rules.why: The structure then carries across themes.

rules.rule: In light themes, alternate white and grey-10 for each added surface layer.
rules.values: Carbon white/gray-10; KRDS gray10 → gray0 → gray5 → gray0

rules.rule: Keep colour near 60% neutrals, 30% secondary and 10% primary for key actions, with accent never above 5%.
Reserve the brand colour for brand elements and the single most important action on the screen.
rules.why: When brand colour is everywhere, nothing stands out.

rules.rule: Use one, maybe two primary colours; give semantic red, yellow and green shades but use them sparingly.
Use colour only where it adds meaning, and use coloured backgrounds sparingly.
rules.why: Key actions and states then stand out.

rules.rule: Make interaction states lighter or darker steps of the same hue; never switch hue for a state.
Offset interaction states by scale steps: hover half a step, selected one step, active two steps.
rules.values: hover 0.5 step; selected 1; active 2 (e.g. Blue 60 → Blue 80)
rules.why: Gives checkable, consistent state deltas.

rules.rule: Give hover, active and focus states more contrast than the rest state.
Separate the logo colour from the UI colour where needed.
rules.values: GOV.UK brand blue #1d70b8 vs link blue #1a65a6

rules.rule: Reserve the focus colour for focus only.
rules.why: Focus is never confused with brand decoration.

rules.rule: On coloured backgrounds, tint borders, shadows and secondary text toward that hue instead of grey.
rules.why: Plain grey looks dirty on colour.

rules.rule: Meet contrast minimums: text 4.5:1, large text 3:1, essential icons and component boundaries 3:1; logos and decoration exempt.
rules.values: text ≥4.5:1; large (≥24px or ≥18.5px bold) ≥3:1; icons/UI boundaries ≥3:1
rules.conflict: Contrast metric: APCA preferred (Vercel, Radix, SEED) vs WCAG 2 ratios (Carbon, GOV.UK, web.dev)

rules.rule: Give focus indicators at least 3:1 contrast.
rules.values: ≥3:1; Carbon 2px Blue 60 border on light themes, white on dark

rules.rule: Never rely on colour alone; pair every status with an icon or text label.
rules.why: A red border alone fails.

rules.rule: Review the page in greyscale to find meaning carried by colour alone.
Do not put high-hue-contrast colours of similar lightness side by side; over images, use static white or black components.
rules.why: They vibrate.

rules.rule: Offer prefers-color-scheme dark and prefers-contrast high-contrast variants; they can be combined.
Pass WCAG 2 AA as the baseline and use APCA as an extra perceptual check.
rules.why: WCAG 2 is the legal baseline; the file's own practical rule.
rules.conflict: Contrast metric: APCA preferred (Vercel, Radix, SEED) vs WCAG 2 ratios (Carbon, GOV.UK, web.dev)

rules.rule: Do not use alpha transparency for disabled states.
rules.why: Contrast becomes unpredictable over varied backgrounds.

rules.rule: Do not invert the light theme; in dark themes closer surfaces are lighter and distant surfaces darker.
rules.values: Carbon: each layer one step lighter; KRDS dark gray90 → gray100 → gray95 → gray90; SEED gray-00/100/200
rules.why: Inversion flips the depth cues.

rules.rule: Avoid #000000 backgrounds and pure white text in dark themes.
rules.values: even #010101 avoids OLED smearing; Superhuman white text at 90% opacity
rules.why: 21:1 causes halation, especially for people with astigmatism.

rules.rule: In dark mode keep the accent hue and lower its lightness.
rules.values: SEED solid fills one shade down (red-700 → red-600); KRDS swaps in a lighter similar hue
rules.conflict: Dark accent: lower lightness + raise saturation (Superhuman) vs subdued shade (web.dev) vs one shade lower (SEED)

rules.rule: Follow KRDS dark-mode minimums: text step 70 (body 90) and icons 70.
rules.values: text 70, body 90, icons 70; system colours icon/text -20, background -95, border -90

rules.rule: Remove or tone down large bright colour blocks in dark sections.
rules.why: They pull focus from content.

rules.rule: After meeting AA, tune perceived contrast by eye for each theme.
Do not make dark components darker than their background, except in high-contrast mode.
Dim photos in dark mode, and swap images such as maps via <picture> with a prefers-color-scheme source.
Store theme colours in custom properties on html, redefine them for dark, and set color-scheme, accent-color and theme-color.
rules.why: Form controls and scrollbars then match the theme.

rules.rule: Disable transitions while switching theme.
rules.why: Otherwise every hover-bound property animates at once.

rules.rule: Use one light source for the whole page: every shadow keeps the same x:y offset ratio.
rules.why: Kennedy: light comes from above.

rules.rule: Give higher elevation a larger offset, larger blur and lower opacity.
Layer shadows from several low-opacity offsets, and do not animate layered shadows.
rules.values: Comeau 5 layers at 1/2/4/8/16px, ~7.5% each; Vercel ≥2 layers + semi-transparent border

rules.rule: Tint shadows with the background hue instead of semi-transparent black, without so much saturation that they glow.
rules.why: Black shadows grey out coloured backgrounds.

rules.rule: Use filter: drop-shadow() for irregular shapes such as cut-out images and tooltips with tails.
To derive a theme from a photo, quantise it, score colours by frequency, hue diversity and chroma, and drop near-greys.
rules.why: Material's dynamic-colour method.

rules.rule: Map a few key colours to roles (primary, secondary, tertiary, error, neutral) and pair each with an on- text colour.
rules.why: Text colours are designed with their fills, not picked later.

rules.rule: Over photos, pick one text-protection method: overlay, translucent box, blur, floor fade or elliptical scrim.
rules.values: overlay e.g. 35% black; floor fade 0% at middle → ~20% black at bottom + slight text shadow
rules.why: Raw text on images only works on dark, low-contrast images tested at every width.

rules.rule: Keep photos consistent in exposure, brightness and contrast so no single image dominates.
Keep UI motion within 100–400ms: about 100ms for simple feedback, 200–300ms for modals, up to 400ms for large moves.
rules.conflict: Max UI duration: Rauno ≤200ms, Kowalski <300ms, NN/g 100–400ms, Carbon up to 400ms (700ms dimming only)

rules.rule: Keep product UI animations under 300ms.
rules.values: Kowalski <300ms (180ms dropdown beats 400ms); Rauno ≤200ms; Carbon micro-interactions 90–120ms
rules.why: Shorter feels more responsive.
rules.conflict: Max UI duration: Rauno ≤200ms, Kowalski <300ms, NN/g 100–400ms, Carbon up to 400ms (700ms dimming only)

rules.rule: Pick duration tokens by job, Carbon style, from fast-01 for toggles up to slow-02 for background dimming only.
rules.values: fast-01 70ms; fast-02 110ms; moderate-01 150ms; moderate-02 240ms; slow-01 400ms; slow-02 700ms
rules.conflict: Max UI duration: Rauno ≤200ms, Kowalski <300ms, NN/g 100–400ms, Carbon up to 400ms (700ms dimming only)

rules.rule: Scale duration with distance and size: small travel is fast, large travel slower (non-linear).
Make entrances slightly longer than exits.
rules.conflict: Enter longer than exit (NN/g) vs hover fast in, slow out, 125/450ms (Comeau)

rules.rule: The more often an animation is seen, the shorter and subtler it should be.
Delay spinners and skeletons before showing them, then keep them visible for a minimum time.
rules.why: Avoids flicker.

rules.rule: Use the shortest duration that does not feel jarring, and test small differences.
rules.why: Animations are more often too long than too short.

rules.rule: Use ease-out for entering or appearing elements.
rules.values: Carbon entrance productive cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.38, 0.9), expressive cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.3, 1)
rules.why: It starts fast, so it feels responsive.
rules.conflict: Exit easing: ease-in for permanent exits (Comeau, Carbon, NN/g) vs ease-out both ways (Kowalski)

rules.rule: Use a standard curve for elements visible throughout the motion; CSS ease is a good general default.
rules.values: Carbon standard productive cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0.38, 0.9), expressive cubic-bezier(0.4, 0.14, 0.3, 1)

rules.rule: Use an accelerating curve for elements leaving for good; a panel that may return uses standard easing.
rules.values: Carbon exit productive cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 1, 0.9), expressive cubic-bezier(0.4, 0.14, 1, 1)
rules.conflict: Exit easing: ease-in for permanent exits (Comeau, Carbon, NN/g) vs ease-out both ways (Kowalski)

rules.rule: Never use linear easing for movement, only for progress or looping rotation; use ease-in-out for loops.
Prefer custom ease-out curves over the weak built-in CSS easings.
Use productive (subtle, fast) motion for task UI and expressive motion only for significant moments.
rules.why: Kowalski: marketing may be expressive, product UI must be fast.

rules.rule: Use springs for position and transform where realism matters, not for colour or opacity; keep CSS transitions when enough.
Animate transform and opacity only where possible; avoid width, height, top, left and margin.
rules.why: Layout properties reflow siblings and drop frames.

rules.rule: Never write transition: all; list the animated properties.
Never scale in from 0; start popovers at about 0.9 or more.
rules.why: Nothing real appears from nothing.
rules.conflict: Start scale ≥0.9, e.g. 0.93 (Kowalski) vs about 0.8 for dialogs (Rauno)

rules.rule: Set transform-origin at the trigger so a popover grows from its button, not the centre.
Make animations interruptible so user input can reverse or cancel them without a jump.
Apply will-change: transform only to elements about to animate, and only during the animation.
rules.why: It costs video memory.

rules.rule: Pause looping animations while they are off-screen.
If a crossfade still looks wrong after tuning, add a small filter: blur() during the swap.
Use motion to show spatial relationships: things enter from where they live and leave toward where they go.
Test animation on the slowest target device.
Give press feedback by scaling to about 0.97 on :active.
rules.conflict: Press scale 0.97 (Kowalski) vs 0.96–0.9 (Rauno)

rules.rule: Wrap hover styles in @media (hover: hover).
rules.why: Otherwise taps leave a sticky hover on touch screens.

rules.rule: Never hide essential content or actions behind hover; pair :hover with :focus-visible.
Do not change font weight, size or case on hover or selection; use colour, background, shadow or underline.
rules.why: It shifts layout.

rules.rule: Keep hover effects from moving the element out from under the cursor; hover the wrapper and animate the child.
rules.why: Otherwise the element flickers.

rules.rule: Delay closing dropdowns on mouse leave, with no delay on enter.
Delay the first tooltip, then show neighbouring tooltips instantly without animation.
Skip hover animation on trivial buttons and other high-frequency elements.
Give decorative glows and gradients pointer-events: none so they do not steal hover.
Make hit targets at least 24px on desktop and 44px on mobile.
Never animate keyboard-initiated actions; consider opening menus on mousedown.
Avoid scrolljacking; if used, keep it short, below the fold, vertical, alternating with normal scroll, with key CTAs above the fold.
rules.why: Users get lost, think the page is broken, and leave.

rules.rule: Keep parallax and scroll-linked motion small relative to the viewport, or skip it, and make it removable.
rules.why: They are vestibular triggers.

rules.rule: Judge motion by its size relative to the screen: a small rotating button is fine, a full-screen wipe is not.
Use scroll-behavior: smooth with scroll-margin-top for anchors, and overscroll-behavior: contain on modals and drawers.
Write motion inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) so browsers without support get none.
rules.why: Comeau rejects the global 0.01ms override.

rules.rule: Under reduced motion, replace movement, zoom and parallax with a fade or no animation.
rules.why: WCAG errata now counts blur as motion.

rules.rule: For JS-driven motion, read matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)') and listen for change.
Swap animated images and background videos for static ones under reduced motion; do not autoplay decorative video.
Give anything that auto-moves for over 5 seconds a pause, stop or hide control; auto-advancing carousels always need one.
Never flash more than 3 times per second, and avoid hard colour cuts.
rules.why: Seizure risk.

rules.rule: Offer a site-level reduce-motion control on animation-heavy pages.
Use motion where it replaces reading on small screens: explain a concept, cover waits with a loop, confirm with a check.
Match motion tone to the news: celebration for good moments, light gentle motion to soften bad news.
Prefer Lottie, and hybrid 3D (rendered PNG frames inside Lottie) over full 3D in-product.
rules.why: Smaller files, no visible quality loss.

rules.rule: Design dark mode and large text into every screen at the system level, not as a retrofit.
Place the logo top-left in left-to-right languages.
rules.why: Right-aligned logos did not seem more distinctive.

rules.rule: Keep the wordmark readable; avoid hard-to-read script names.
rules.why: Hard-to-read names were remembered much less.

rules.rule: Prepare logo lockups for different contexts, make the symbol work alone at small sizes, and keep known elements in a refresh.
rules.why: Keeps existing recognition.

rules.rule: Brand colours may be borrowed from a parent palette, and a strong symbol can sit on coloured backgrounds.
rules.values: GDS took cyan and midnight blue from the DSIT palette

rules.rule: Roll out a brand refresh in stages and lead with the mission rather than colour.
rules.values: Baemin 2.0: app icon first, colour and WORK체 two weeks later
rules.why: Gradual change avoids alienating users.

rules.rule: Show real people and real products, not generic stock people.
rules.values: real staff portraits +10% viewing time vs bios taking 316% more space
rules.why: Generic stock people are ignored.
rules.conflict: AI images perform like stock (NN/g S40), but generic stock is ignored (S39); suspected AI lowers ratings

rules.rule: Give informative images (product, people, process) the most space, drop feel-good filler, enlarge to at least 2× thumbnail.
Choose image type by content: photos for products, places and people; illustration for abstract services; icons for actions.
Hide all text and check that the images alone still give the right mood.
Pair rich imagery with text-heavy layouts and simple imagery with airy layouts.
Keep one illustration style, and give icons one stroke weight matched to the font, one corner style and fill.
If full illustration is out of reach, use illustration only on edge states (404, empty, onboarding, error).
Make a mascot reflect what the product actually does.
rules.why: Otherwise the warmth feels hollow.

rules.rule: Before using an AI hero image, check hands, text, screens, reflections, backgrounds and representation.
rules.values: scored about the same as stock; only authenticity significant (~+0.4/7)
rules.why: Users who suspected AI rated the site lower.
rules.conflict: AI images perform like stock (NN/g S40), but generic stock is ignored (S39); suspected AI lowers ratings

rules.rule: For a small business, rely on its own photos, a legible logo in the usual spot, one sparing brand colour and one image style.
rules.why: Synthesis of several sources; none covers small business directly.

rules.rule: Do not make shades with lighten()/darken() or black/white overlays; use a tuned scale.
rules.why: They come out muddy and uneven.

rules.rule: Do not switch hue for hover or active states, or add one-off colours outside the palette.
Do not spread the brand or accent colour everywhere, such as accent well above 5% or brand colour on many buttons.
Do not use pure #000 backgrounds with pure white text, or a simply inverted light theme.
rules.why: Depth gets flipped.

rules.rule: Avoid large bright colour blocks in dark sections.
Avoid flat grey or black shadows on coloured backgrounds, and over-saturated shadows that read as glows.
Keep shadow angles consistent across cards and buttons.
Avoid vibrating neighbours: saturated hues of equal lightness side by side.
Do not show status by colour alone, such as a red border or a green dot without a label.
Do not scale things in from 0, grow popovers from their centre, or squash buttons to 0.8 on press.
rules.conflict: Start scale ≥0.9, e.g. 0.93 (Kowalski) vs about 0.8 for dialogs (Rauno); Press scale 0.97 (Kowalski) vs 0.96–0.9 (Rauno)

rules.rule: Avoid transition: all, animated width/height/top, and animated layered shadows.
Avoid durations of 400–500ms+ on everyday UI and ease-in or linear movement on interface elements.
rules.values: 400–500ms+ is too long for everyday UI
rules.conflict: Max UI duration: Rauno ≤200ms, Kowalski <300ms, NN/g 100–400ms, Carbon up to 400ms (700ms dimming only); Exit easing: ease-in for permanent exits (Comeau, Carbon, NN/g) vs ease-out both ways (Kowalski)

rules.rule: Avoid hover animation on every trivial button, delight animation on frequent actions, and animated keyboard actions.
Avoid font-weight jumps on hover and hover effects that slide the target away from the cursor.
Do not leave hover styles outside (hover: hover); they stick after taps on phones.
