Do not let decorative glows and gradient overlays block hover.
Do not leave gradient text gradient when it is selected.
Avoid parallax, scroll-jacked storytelling above the fold, and auto-advancing carousels with no pause.
Do not ignore prefers-reduced-motion or rely on a global 0.01ms override.
Avoid generic stock people, feel-good decoration photos, and AI images with broken hands, text or reflections.
rules.conflict: AI images perform like stock (NN/g S40), but generic stock is ignored (S39); suspected AI lowers ratings

rules.rule: Do not mix illustration styles, or icons with mismatched stroke and fill.
Do not centre or right-align the logo to look different; it adds no distinctiveness and lowers recall.
Lay out the page in greyscale first and add colour last, on purpose.
rules.why: Spacing, size and order problems surface before colour hides them.

rules.rule: Copy great work only in private studies, and publish only original work.
rules.why: Public near-copies cost opportunities and are unethical to show.
rules.conflict: Copying: Kennedy imitate the best vs Hische copy only in private vs Boag do not copy competitors at all

rules.rule: Draw from many references, including historical ones, never just one or two.
rules.why: A single source shows through as a blend of that one designer.

rules.rule: Before showing a design, ask whether it looks like someone you know, and move away if it does.
rules.why: Derivative work is recognisable.
rules.conflict: Copying: Kennedy imitate the best vs Hische copy only in private vs Boag do not copy competitors at all

rules.rule: Look for ideas outside the client's sector.
rules.why: Competitors copy each other; better patterns often live elsewhere.
rules.conflict: Copying: Kennedy imitate the best vs Hische copy only in private vs Boag do not copy competitors at all

rules.rule: Treat competitor sites as inputs, never instructions, and distrust the argument that everyone in the sector does X.
rules.why: Competitors often have not researched their choices.
rules.conflict: Copying: Kennedy imitate the best vs Hische copy only in private vs Boag do not copy competitors at all

rules.rule: Imitate the best work until you are good, and let a personal style emerge later.
rules.why: Chasing a style before fundamentals produces weak work.
rules.conflict: Copying: Kennedy imitate the best vs Hische copy only in private vs Boag do not copy competitors at all

rules.rule: When admired work succeeds, explain why in words, not just good or bad.
rules.why: Taste is trained pattern reading and can be transferred, even to agents.
rules.conflict: Taste vs principles: Friedman says written principles decide vs Kowalski, van Schneider, Hische: taste is core

rules.rule: Give an agent one strict rule file per aspect with exact values, then have it review its output with before/after.
rules.why: Without exact rules it guesses or invents standards.

rules.rule: Review motion, radii and other fine details again the next day with fresh eyes.
rules.why: First-day judgement is unreliable.

rules.rule: Write principles that say what you will not do, as 'we want X because Y', and test them on real screens.
rules.why: Vague principles cannot be applied and lead to dull work.
rules.conflict: Taste vs principles: Friedman says written principles decide vs Kowalski, van Schneider, Hische: taste is core

rules.rule: Start from an analogy, extract its qualities, then drop the analogy and keep the rules.
rules.why: Turns a mood into checkable criteria.

rules.rule: Question whether a section should exist before polishing it, and show the core idea to real users early.
rules.why: Late discovery is expensive.

rules.rule: Pick a direction and own it rather than averaging everyone's feedback.
rules.why: Consensus designs come out bland.
rules.conflict: Taste vs principles: Friedman says written principles decide vs Kowalski, van Schneider, Hische: taste is core

rules.rule: In a critique, look past the visuals to copy, navigation, hierarchy and accessibility.
rules.why: 'How could it work better' finds more than 'look better'.

rules.rule: List the real requirements first and shape the design to what plain HTML and CSS do well; add no unneeded tooling.
rules.why: Small sites drown in the overhead.
rules.conflict: Tooling: Chimero plain HTML/CSS for small sites vs design-system tokens and pipelines that assume scale

rules.rule: Choose a typeface only after understanding the job, from a shortlist of suitable candidates.
rules.why: A default chosen by elimination is a thoughtless default.
rules.conflict: Fonts: Kennedy steers to neutral free sans vs Santa Maria: neutral defaults by elimination are the problem

rules.rule: Start from generous whitespace, roughly doubling what feels enough.
rules.values: menu items ~2× text height; ~25px between list groups
rules.why: Unstyled defaults are cramped; space creates hierarchy.

rules.rule: Use three spacing tiers: between lines, between elements, and larger between groups.
rules.why: Gap size tells viewers what belongs together.

rules.rule: Use a 12-column marketing grid of 64px columns and 32px gutters in a 1120px container.
rules.values: 12 × 64px, 32px gutters, 1120px container (>1280px viewport); 16px group / 32px separate; mobile 32px margins, 1 column, 24px gap
rules.why: 12 divides into 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6 columns.
rules.conflict: Grids: Kennedy skips column grids and ratio scales vs Malewicz 12-col 64/32px grid vs WIG align to grid/baseline

rules.rule: Let content set its width and align elements to each other rather than forcing fixed columns.
rules.why: Rigid grids break on resizing screens.
rules.conflict: Grids: Kennedy skips column grids and ratio scales vs Malewicz 12-col 64/32px grid vs WIG align to grid/baseline

rules.rule: Build the page up from its content, then size the container; do not cram content into a fixed frame.
rules.why: The web has no fixed edges.

rules.rule: Default to stacked full-width bands and plan for text beside an image as the window widens.
rules.why: A fixed-ratio image grows taller while the text column shrinks.

rules.rule: Use fluid percentage widths, and re-check column count, type size and tap targets at each breakpoint.
rules.why: Layouts must survive unknown viewports.

rules.rule: Break up long pages with recurring interludes (big type, full photo, colour field, pull quote) in one visual system.
rules.why: Rhythm keeps people reading.

rules.rule: Align every element to something, and nudge by ±1px where the eye disagrees with the geometry.
rules.why: Perceived alignment matters more than numeric.
rules.conflict: Grids: Kennedy skips column grids and ratio scales vs Malewicz 12-col 64/32px grid vs WIG align to grid/baseline

rules.rule: Check every layout at mobile, laptop and ultra-wide, with short, average and very long content.
rules.why: Real content breaks the ideal mockup.

rules.rule: Make nested radii concentric: inner radius = outer radius − padding; if that is ≤0, use 1–4px or raise the outer.
rules.why: Mismatched radii look amateur.

rules.rule: Rank elements by importance and make visibility follow that order through size, colour, contrast and weight.
rules.why: Attention is the job.

rules.rule: Fully emphasise only the page title; mix up and down levers on every other element.
rules.values: e.g. big number in a light weight; small bold caps label with tracking
rules.why: Maxing every lever flattens hierarchy.

rules.rule: Drop labels when the format shows what the data is; otherwise fold the label into the value.
rules.why: 'label: value' gives everything the same weight.

rules.rule: When labels must stay, make them quieter than the value, except on spec sheets where people scan for labels.
rules.why: Emphasis should follow what the reader looks for.

rules.rule: Reserve underline for links, and avoid highlight backgrounds and strikethrough for emphasis.
rules.why: They read as links, hover states or deletions.

rules.rule: Change colour, background, shadow or underline on hover and selection, never size, weight or case.
rules.why: Those reflow the text and make the layout jump.

rules.rule: Make hover, active and focus states contrast more than the resting state.
rules.why: Feedback has to be visible.

rules.rule: Set body text at 18–24px on reading pages and 14–20px on interaction-heavy pages; 16–20px on mobile.
rules.why: Readable defaults beat tiny 'elegant' text.

rules.rule: Set page titles at 35–50px on desktop and 28–40px on mobile, in bold or heavier.
rules.why: Headings are the best place for a second font.

rules.rule: Use about four type sizes, with secondary text about 2px smaller at about 70% colour strength.
rules.why: Fewer sizes look intentional.

rules.rule: Size type levels by how distinct they must be, with bigger jumps at large sizes, not by a ratio scale.
rules.why: Mathematical scales do not fix weak hierarchy.
rules.conflict: Grids: Kennedy skips column grids and ratio scales vs Malewicz 12-col 64/32px grid vs WIG align to grid/baseline

rules.rule: Keep line length at 50–75 characters, and reduce the size if mobile lines fall below about 30.
rules.why: Comprehension drops outside that band.

rules.rule: Tighten tracking as size grows: positive at small sizes, about −1% to −2% at display sizes.
rules.why: Big type at default spacing looks loose and cheap.

rules.rule: Loosen the letter-spacing on small uppercase labels.
rules.why: Tight caps are hard to read.

rules.rule: Use tabular figures for prices and columns, curly quotes, a single … character, no widows, and nbsp before units.
rules.why: Cheap markers of care.

rules.rule: Pick fallback fonts with matching metrics, and preload and subset the main font.
rules.why: Avoids layout shift while fonts load.

rules.rule: Prefer clean, well-made neutral fonts over decorative ones, avoid overused picks like Montserrat and the thinnest weights.
rules.values: e.g. Satoshi, Metropolis, Source Sans, Figtree
rules.why: Decorative fonts are hard to control; light weights fail on screens.
rules.conflict: Fonts: Kennedy steers to neutral free sans vs Santa Maria: neutral defaults by elimination are the problem

rules.rule: Let the typeface echo the brand motif, such as letterforms that match the logo shape.
rules.why: Ties the type to the brand.

rules.rule: Highlight a headline phrase with a font change, width change or thick brand-coloured underline.
rules.why: Adds character without new decoration.

rules.rule: Build the palette from one base colour and derive its variants; skip colour-wheel harmonies.
rules.why: Those schemes do not predict good UI.
rules.conflict: Colour: Kennedy one base hue, no harmonies vs Malewicz 60-30-10 across hues vs Refactoring UI multi-hue ramps

rules.rule: For darker shades lower brightness and raise saturation; for lighter shades raise brightness and lower saturation.
rules.why: Brightness-only darkening looks muddy (~95% of the time).

rules.rule: Shift hue slightly with lightness to keep shades vivid and to tune personality.
rules.values: dark → 0/120/240°, light → 60/180/300°; blue 240°→210° casual, →260° indigo; error red toward pink
rules.why: Small hue moves change personality.

rules.rule: Define fixed ramps up front: 8–10 greys, 1–2 primaries with 5–10 shades each, and a few state accents.
rules.values: 8–10 greys; 1–2 primaries × 5–10 shades; pick 500, then 900/100, then fill in
rules.why: Shades made on the fly with lighten/darken drift and multiply.
rules.conflict: Colour: Kennedy one base hue, no harmonies vs Malewicz 60-30-10 across hues vs Refactoring UI multi-hue ramps

rules.rule: Start greys at a dark grey, not black, and tint them slightly toward the brand hue.
rules.values: more saturation in the darker greys
rules.why: Fully neutral greys look dead.

rules.rule: Tint borders, shadows and secondary text toward the background hue.
rules.why: Pure black shadows and grey borders look pasted on.

rules.rule: Split colour roughly 60% dominant, 30% secondary, 10% accent, keeping the vivid accent for the main action.
rules.why: The eye goes to the rarest, brightest colour.
rules.conflict: Colour: Kennedy one base hue, no harmonies vs Malewicz 60-30-10 across hues vs Refactoring UI multi-hue ramps

rules.rule: Tone down an overpowering brand colour by lowering its saturation, not changing its hue.
rules.why: It stays on brand but stops shouting.

rules.rule: Avoid oversaturated colours in dark mode.
rules.why: They vibrate and strain the eye.

rules.rule: Never show status by colour alone; add a text label.
rules.why: Colour-blind users miss it.

rules.rule: Light from above: raised elements get a lighter top and darker bottom; inset elements get the opposite.
rules.why: Depth tells people what they can press.
rules.conflict: Depth: Kennedy against pure flat, top-lit shadows vs Chimero: flat colour is a web-native response

rules.rule: Prefer flat-ish over purely flat, and keep subtle shadows.
rules.why: Removing every depth cue hurts style and meaning.
rules.conflict: Depth: Kennedy against pure flat, top-lit shadows vs Chimero: flat colour is a web-native response

rules.rule: Build shadows from at least two layers (ambient and direct) and pair them with a semi-transparent border.
rules.why: One-layer shadows look like a default.

rules.rule: Give shadows and effects a meaning (depth, interactivity), not decoration.
rules.why: Decoration without meaning reads as noise.
rules.conflict: Decoration: Kennedy adds accents vs Chimero 'bicycle bear' warning vs Lovin meaning only; agree on few, on-motif

rules.rule: Pick one motif and repeat it across logo, type, dividers, bullets and numbers; add motif, not decoration.
rules.why: The main way a site feels like one brand, not a template.
rules.conflict: Decoration: Kennedy adds accents vs Chimero 'bicycle bear' warning vs Lovin meaning only; agree on few, on-motif

rules.rule: Add only a few accents to a solid base, such as angled edges, brand bullets, breakouts, a faint dot grid or offset shadows.
rules.why: Plain defaults look generic; piling effects looks worse.
rules.conflict: Decoration: Kennedy adds accents vs Chimero 'bicycle bear' warning vs Lovin meaning only; agree on few, on-motif

rules.rule: Keep textures faint and use only effects that match the brand motif.
rules.why: Arbitrary effects feel bolted on.
rules.conflict: Decoration: Kennedy adds accents vs Chimero 'bicycle bear' warning vs Lovin meaning only; agree on few, on-motif

rules.rule: Let a small detail carry meaning, such as drop caps cut to echo the story's subject.
rules.why: Specific details make a page belong to its content.

rules.rule: Invest in the small conveniences users would miss if they vanished.
rules.why: Details build loyalty more than features.

rules.rule: Protect text over photos with an overlay, translucent box, blur, floor fade or scrim; test raw text at every size.
rules.values: 35% black overlay; floor fade 0% at middle → ~20% at bottom
rules.why: Legibility breaks when the image or viewport changes.

rules.rule: Do not rely on one photo's natural blur for text legibility.
rules.why: Swap the image and the text breaks.

rules.rule: Set image dimensions, preload only above-the-fold images, lazy-load the rest, and prefer muted looping video to GIFs.
rules.why: Layout shift and slow heroes feel cheap.

rules.rule: Let images scale with their containers, but cap them so wide screens do not push the text away.
Keep most UI motion under 300ms, exits about 20% faster than entrances, and longer for bigger moves.
rules.values: micro 100–150ms; standard 150–250ms; modals/drawers 200–300ms; exits ~20% faster; 180ms dropdown beats 400ms
rules.why: Slow motion on frequent actions reads as lag.
rules.conflict: Motion: Kowalski/Freiberg cut frequent motion, <300ms vs Kowalski allows slower, richer motion on marketing pages

rules.rule: Use ease-out to enter or leave, ease-in-out for on-screen moves, ease for hover, and linear only for constant motion.
rules.why: Ease-out's fast start feels responsive.

rules.rule: Scale to 0.97 on :active, and start entrances at 0.9–0.95, never 0.
rules.why: Things should not appear from nowhere.

rules.rule: Set transform-origin to the trigger so a popover grows from its button.
rules.why: Spatial origin explains cause and effect.

rules.rule: Animate only transform and opacity, never transition: all, and provide a prefers-reduced-motion variant.
rules.why: Layout properties drop frames; some users get motion sick.

rules.rule: Do not animate frequent actions (menus, command palettes, dense hover) or keyboard actions; keep delight for rare moments.
rules.why: Repeated delight becomes friction.
rules.conflict: Motion: Kowalski/Freiberg cut frequent motion, <300ms vs Kowalski allows slower, richer motion on marketing pages

rules.rule: Make every animation interruptible; user input wins over motion.
rules.why: Locked transitions feel broken.

rules.rule: Delay the first tooltip; once one is open, show its neighbours instantly with no animation.
rules.why: Prevents accidental popups without slowing exploration.

rules.rule: Add a slight blur during a crossfade when easing and timing cannot hide it.
rules.why: The blur masks the gap between states.

rules.rule: Allow slower, richer motion on marketing pages than in app UI.
rules.why: Speed rules matter most for repeated actions.
rules.conflict: Motion: Kowalski/Freiberg cut frequent motion, <300ms vs Kowalski allows slower, richer motion on marketing pages

rules.rule: Autoplay only muted, non-essential loops, and give anything longer than 5 seconds a pause control.
Give spinners and skeletons a show delay and a minimum visible time, and match skeletons to the final layout.
rules.why: Avoids flashes and jumps.

rules.rule: Make tap targets at least 44px on mobile and 24px on desktop, with the hit area matching the visual.
Make anything that looks clickable clickable, and use real <a> elements for links.
rules.why: New-tab and right-click then work.

rules.rule: Keep submit enabled until submission, show a spinner with the label, put errors by fields and focus the first.
rules.why: Never block typing.

rules.rule: Make destructive actions confirmable or undoable, and explain failures plainly with a next step.
Design empty, sparse, dense and error states, not just the ideal one.
Make primary actions reachable one-handed on mobile.
rules.why: People use small-business sites on the go.

rules.rule: Make behaviour match the visual polish.
rules.why: A slick page primes users to expect it to work as well.

rules.rule: Put frequent controls near corners and screen edges, which act as infinite targets.
rules.why: Fitts's law.

rules.rule: Render the first screen fast, respond within milliseconds, and show progress when something is slow.
Write button labels that say exactly what happens, and frame errors with how to fix them.
Fold context into values instead of using labels.
rules.why: Shorter, warmer copy and clearer hierarchy.

rules.rule: Prefer inline help, and use tooltips as a last resort.
rules.why: Hidden help is rarely found.

rules.rule: Use text as interface where it fits.
rules.why: Chimero lists it among web-native patterns.

rules.rule: Build character from how ordinary things are done, not from complexity.
rules.why: A simple move done your own way beats an elaborate borrowed one.
rules.conflict: Taste vs principles: Friedman says written principles decide vs Kowalski, van Schneider, Hische: taste is core

rules.rule: Treat quality as a deliberate, costly choice; judge work by how it feels, performs and ages.
Remove features or sections that no longer serve the vision, even if they were requested.
rules.why: Restraint signals intent.

rules.rule: Aim for clarity, not just simplicity: frame and explain complex offers instead of stripping them bare.
Lead with a clear point of view that comes across in a quick scroll, rather than trying to be complete.
Keep the experience coherent across every surface: pages, emails and print.
rules.why: World-building separates great designers from good ones.

rules.rule: Escape unstyled defaults: small text, no line spacing, content running to the edge.
rules.why: Starting from them produces cramped pages.

rules.rule: Do not use too many colours in too many places.
rules.why: It destroys a clean look.

rules.rule: Avoid purely flat design with no light or depth.
rules.conflict: Depth: Kennedy against pure flat, top-lit shadows vs Chimero: flat colour is a web-native response

rules.rule: Swap a few default-looking parts (stock bullets, boxy splits) for brand versions, without stacking effects.
rules.why: Default parts read as boring.
rules.conflict: Decoration: Kennedy adds accents vs Chimero 'bicycle bear' warning vs Lovin meaning only; agree on few, on-motif

rules.rule: Do not decorate without a motif; repeat one idea everywhere instead.
rules.why: Decoration without a motif feels arbitrary.
rules.conflict: Decoration: Kennedy adds accents vs Chimero 'bicycle bear' warning vs Lovin meaning only; agree on few, on-motif

rules.rule: Avoid overused fonts such as Montserrat and thoughtless defaults chosen by elimination.
rules.conflict: Fonts: Kennedy steers to neutral free sans vs Santa Maria: neutral defaults by elimination are the problem

rules.rule: Choose web patterns (big bands, blurred photo with big type, device mockups, mosaics) for the content, not by habit.
rules.why: Flashy 'bicycle bear' sites impress briefly, then fail.
rules.conflict: Decoration: Kennedy adds accents vs Chimero 'bicycle bear' warning vs Lovin meaning only; agree on few, on-motif

rules.rule: Treat 'everyone in our sector uses this structure' as a red flag; copying competitors gives mediocre results.
rules.conflict: Copying: Kennedy imitate the best vs Hische copy only in private vs Boag do not copy competitors at all

rules.rule: Avoid work that looks like one known designer.
rules.why: It silently costs opportunities.
rules.conflict: Copying: Kennedy imitate the best vs Hische copy only in private vs Boag do not copy competitors at all

rules.rule: Decide what is worth building and which values it expresses; without principles, fast-generated work looks random.
Give agents strict written rules with exact values; without them they invent motion and type standards.
Resist disposable, fast-made output; convenience culture dulls the ability to recognise quality.
Cut animations without a purpose and delight that repeats daily.
rules.why: Repeated delight turns into friction.
rules.conflict: Motion: Kowalski/Freiberg cut frequent motion, <300ms vs Kowalski allows slower, richer motion on marketing pages

rules.rule: Write every product string in 해요체 and keep one voice across the whole site.
rules.why: Users experience the service as one speaker.
rules.conflict: Toss: one voice for 40+ services vs KB: one voice, tone per channel (terse in payments, playful in events)

rules.rule: Drop stiff honorifics (~시, 계시다, 여쭈다, 께) by default; keep them for the user's situation, guesses or favours asked.
rules.why: Default copy should be casual and polite, not ceremonial.

rules.rule: Use active, positive sentences, and use negatives only when something is unavailable, with the reason.
rules.values: '있어요', not '없지 않아요'; passive only for ending/expiry or reassurance

rules.rule: Make the button label, or the line above it, say what happens next.
rules.why: A button that silently opened a survey made users uneasy.

rules.rule: End a single CTA in ~하기, use 확인/다음 for steps, and 닫기/다음에, not 취소, to dismiss a two-button dialog.
rules.why: '취소' reads as cancelling the task in progress.

rules.rule: Keep bottom-sheet and modal titles to one line.
Cut filler words: if deleting a word leaves the meaning unchanged, delete it.
rules.why: Remove filler, not shorten for its own sake.

rules.rule: Do not add sentences because the layout looks empty, and do not repeat the title in the body.
Show only what the user needs at this step; with two options, state the real difference between them.
Write as people talk: everyday words, one message per sentence, few 한자어 compounds; read it aloud to test.
rules.conflict: Toss 'Zero Jargon', break up 한자어 vs KB keep the term + explain; regulated terms follow KB

rules.rule: Suggest rather than push: no loss threats ('놓치면 손해'), pleading or guilt-trip copy or graphics.
rules.why: Keep the benefit and facts; leave the choice with the user.
rules.conflict: Toss: congratulate the user's hidden emotion, but no emotional pleading; recognise, never guilt

rules.rule: Avoid slang, memes and terms that only one age group or trade understands.
Acknowledge the user's effort or feeling at key moments, not just the system state.
rules.why: Toss saw much better metrics after recognising repayment effort.
rules.conflict: Toss: congratulate the user's hidden emotion, but no emotional pleading; recognise, never guilt

rules.rule: Give every error message at least its cause, then a fix.
rules.why: Never leave users guessing by trial and error.

rules.rule: Make status labels show progress, and cut internal states down to the ones the user cares about.
rules.values: e.g. 9 → 3: 처리 중 / 해외 은행 도착 / 완료

rules.rule: Echo cryptic input back in human terms, and use guided selection where typos are costly.
Turn jargon into plain words, but keep a term with a short explanation if plain words change the meaning.
rules.conflict: Toss 'Zero Jargon', break up 한자어 vs KB keep the term + explain; regulated terms follow KB

rules.rule: Never use exaggerated or misleading copy to raise clicks.
Lead with the value, then ask for the action, and say why an input is needed.
Build the voice from patterns in existing good copy, and get the team to agree before writing a guideline.
rules.why: An unwanted guideline goes unused.

rules.rule: Pick the headline message from the customer's real worry, not the feature list.
rules.why: Fear of not knowing beat price.

rules.rule: Use a typeface made for screens; test any print-era Hangul face on screen before using it for body text.
rules.why: Apple Gothic drew readability complaints on early iPhones.

rules.rule: Keep display or ornate faces at large headline sizes, off small sizes and low-resolution screens.
rules.why: Fine details break at low resolution.

rules.rule: When a family is split by optical size (Display/Text), pick the cut by set size, not by weight.
rules.conflict: Most Korean families ship by weight vs 노은유 Display/Text cuts; choose by size first

rules.rule: Default to Pretendard (OFL) for UI, load its dynamic subset, and set the variable weight range in Next.js.
rules.why: Matches Apple SD 산돌고딕 Neo spacing and SF heights.
rules.conflict: Neutral type (TPS, Pretendard) vs 배민 rule-breaking type; keep rule-breaking at display sizes, neutral body; Pretendard needs no extra tracking vs common negative body tracking (~-0.3, unverified); default none on body

rules.rule: Use tabular figures (tnum) for prices, dates, tables and live numbers; proportional figures for a single hero number.
Check mixed Hangul–Latin–digit lines, and pick a font that balances the scripts instead of patching each element.
rules.why: Digits and Latin often look small and thin beside Hangul.

rules.rule: Check that %, +/−, ₩, arrows and brackets sit centred and evenly spaced in buttons and price rows.
Check text centring inside buttons on Windows/Chrome as well as iOS/Safari.
rules.why: Hangul vertical metrics differ by OS.

rules.rule: Make sure the font covers all 11,172 Hangul syllables or loads a fallback.
rules.values: 11,172 syllables; the 2,350-char KS set breaks on names and chat

rules.rule: Use one middle dot code point and one ellipsis style across the site.
rules.values: · U+00B7; Pretendard ss05 for a Korean-style ellipsis

rules.rule: Keep two body text styles: Compact with tight leading for UI, Body with about 160% leading for running text.
rules.why: Avoids a new style for every component.

rules.rule: Name text sizes to grow both ways: body sm/md/lg around md, headings 01, 02… counting up from the body base.
Keep a brand display face (배민 style) for marketing and headline moments, not body text.
rules.why: Its deliberate irregularity hurts readability at reading sizes.
rules.conflict: Neutral type (TPS, Pretendard) vs 배민 rule-breaking type; keep rule-breaking at display sizes, neutral body

rules.rule: When borrowing from Korean street signage, follow the original tool and material, and make the quirks systematic.
rules.conflict: Neutral type (TPS, Pretendard) vs 배민 rule-breaking type; keep rule-breaking at display sizes, neutral body

rules.rule: Give one page one main job, and make the next action obvious at a glance.
rules.conflict: Toss keypad-first leaves little business room vs Naver balances owners and avoids drastic simplification

rules.rule: Merge scattered lookups into one chronological or unified list when users want the overview.
On crowded screens keep the user's own data in the main layer, and put suggestions in a smaller collapsible layer.
rules.values: structural change ~3× CTR/CVR vs 1.1× from restyling

rules.rule: Before restyling, ask whether the problem is structural.
Keep graphics from pushing key information below the fold, and size them to the information density.
Align at the pixel level; small misalignments make a screen feel assembled rather than designed.
Build from shared components and tokens so every page looks and behaves the same.
rules.why: Per-page rebuilds create inconsistency and design debt.

rules.rule: Add features or sections only as a last resort.
rules.why: Every extra block adds complexity.
rules.conflict: Toss keypad-first leaves little business room vs Naver balances owners and avoids drastic simplification

rules.rule: On a site many depend on, move things cautiously and serve sub-groups in their own corner.
rules.why: Even one moved button affects people who rely on it.
rules.conflict: Toss keypad-first leaves little business room vs Naver balances owners and avoids drastic simplification

rules.rule: Make the service usable by everyone, including older users and people left out of digital services.
Keep functional UI from looking like an ad: strip colour and illustration from anything that is the user's information.
rules.conflict: Remove graphics for information (김현지) vs build the screen around a character (고명은); decided by the block's job

rules.rule: Add finish with restraint (corner smoothing, a translucent surface, a faint button gradient) and avoid loud colour.
Use no decorative filler, and only one fitting icon or emoji at a time.
rules.conflict: Remove graphics for information (김현지) vs build the screen around a character (고명은); decided by the block's job

rules.rule: Take the accent from the brand or logo colour, and use mid-tones for graphics on light and dark backgrounds.
Name colour tokens by element, intent, emphasis and state, with brand colour under chromatic.
rules.why: Brand colour can change strength without new names.

rules.rule: Test every illustration at its smallest size, keeping face and silhouette readable.
When a mascot is the focus, rebuild the layout around it, ground it with a shadow, and reuse its icon language.
rules.why: Dropped onto a stock layout it reads as a sticker.
rules.conflict: Remove graphics for information (김현지) vs build the screen around a character (고명은); decided by the block's job

rules.rule: For an illustration series, fix the shared style and vary only named slots; review the set side by side.
Define the business in one or two plain sentences before visuals, and reuse its keywords in name, intro and headings.
Plan how the mark works across the website, signage, business cards and the space together.
rules.why: Branding is not only a logo.

rules.rule: Collect a real brief (business type, name meaning, interior, story, style) and design from the story.
Keep a small brand's mark simple and lasting; for multi-product shops, express the value, not one product.
Do not define the audience too narrowly in the slogan.
Show price, address, hours and account or bank names in human-readable, verifiable form.
rules.why: Reassurance beats cleverness (generalised from P6).

rules.rule: Present each case as problem, approach and why, result, then what changed.
Show judgment, not just screens: service, operations and data decisions.
Let the team feel the user's problem first-hand; interview quotes alone rarely move priorities.
Back decisions with data and user feedback, but keep human judgment for brand-sensitive copy.
Do not pad empty-looking layouts with sentences that repeat the title.
Cut meaningless decoration: stock illustrations, particles, heavy gradients, icons on every line, false warning icons.
rules.conflict: Remove graphics for information (김현지) vs build the screen around a character (고명은); decided by the block's job

rules.rule: Avoid loud, graphic-heavy blocks in functional areas; they read as ads and get skipped.
rules.conflict: Remove graphics for information (김현지) vs build the screen around a character (고명은); decided by the block's job

rules.rule: Do not drop a mascot or image onto a stock layout; it looks like a sticker.
Fix pixel-level misalignment; it makes a page feel assembled.
Treat AI output as raw material, and decide what to keep, cut and refine.
Avoid stiff, formulaic logos by designing from the shop's story.
Do not reduce branding to a logo draft; include the mission and a touchpoint plan.
Make one type decision instead of piling up mismatched fonts and per-element patches.
Avoid print fonts on screen and display fonts at body size.
Ban pressure copy such as loss threats and pleading.
Avoid the default AI page (centred headline, subtitle, 3–4 feature cards, testimonials); change colour, font, radius, shadow.
rules.why: Traced to shadcn/ui defaults.
